join_split.turned_shapes_into_a_live_sha: Turned {n} shapes into a live shape (Split into separate shapes gives them back)

join_split.made_complete_n: {n} complete shapes now: their notes follow their own lines

image.kinds_all: PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, BMP or TIFF
image.player_tip: Your player's window size and how many keys it shows across (Falling notes) or up (Piano roll). The outline is as many px in the player's window: the preview is a different size, so it draws the outline thinner or thicker to look the same.
image.shade: Shading (bright to dark across the key)
image.look_note: The look only changes the preview, so it matches the player you use. "Join same-colour notes" changes the notes too: joined = fewer, longer notes.
image.cancelled: Cancelled: the image and its settings are back as they were.

paste.title: Paste colours

paste.lock: Lock them: the image uses exactly these colours (right-click a colour later to free it)
paste.start: Only a starting point: Spiderweb may change them to fit the image better
paste.ch10_left: Channel 10 isn't used (drums): the image gets the other 15.
image.share_note: {n} other placed image(s) share these colours. More share = this image gets the better colours when they compete.
image.share_alone: Share only matters with other images placed (they all share one set of colours).
image.others_missing: ({n} other image(s) couldn't be read: their colours may shift)

image.panel: An image: {value:,} notes. Double-click it to change its look. Drag a corner or side to resize it (its notes are made again from the image, sharp), just outside a corner to turn it, just outside a side's middle to skew it.
image.label: {name}  ·  {keys} keys  ·  {colours} colours  ·  double-click: look
image.menu_own_shape: Back to the image's own shape
image.swatch_tip: Click a colour to pick it yourself: it stays as you picked it (corner mark). Right-click: let Spiderweb pick it again.
app.tools_list_tip: Every drawing tool. Pick one and this button shows it, so one click picks it again. The pin on a tool's right gives it its own button here.
app.pin_tip: Pin: give this tool its own button in the toolbar. Click again to take the button away.
app.keeps_overlaps_every_note_exactly_as:
Keeps overlaps.
Every note exactly as the shapes make it, all on one channel.
Notes on the same key can overlap or start on the same tick.
app.removes_overlaps_all_on_one_channel:
Removes overlaps, all on one channel.
Where two notes on the same key overlap, the earlier one is cut
where the later one starts, and the later one is stretched
to where the earlier one would have ended.
Notes starting on the same tick become one note: the loudest wins,
and it's as long as the longest of them.
app.a_channel_per_overlap_shapes_whose:
A channel per overlap.
Shapes whose notes overlap go on different channels, each on its own
track (channel 10 is skipped). Shapes that don't clash share a channel.
The box below picks what counts as an overlap.
app.split_same_key_at_the_same: Split: same key at the same time
app.split_any_notes_at_the_same: Split: any notes at the same time
app.same_key_shapes_only_get_split:
Same key: shapes only get split when they play the same key at the same time.
Any notes: shapes get split whenever their notes play at the same time,
even on different keys (e.g. two parallel lines, or lines starting on the
same tick). Shapes that follow one after another still share a channel.
snap.tip:
The grid points and notes snap to while you draw and drag (Shift = don't snap).
Note lengths: 1/4 = a quarter note (one beat), 3/8 = a dotted quarter, 1/6 = quarter-note triplets.
Custom… = any length you set up.
snap.kind_tip:
Empty = one plain note (16 = a 16th note), the left number isn't used.
/ = that many notes (3 / 16 = three 16th notes).
. = a dotted note (one and a half notes), .. = double dotted (one and three quarters).
snap.divided_by_tip: Splits the length into this many equal steps (3 = triplets).
app.history_tip: The History list: every change as a step; click one to go back to it.
app.every_tip_searchable_opens_at_the: Every tip, searchable. Opens at the tool you're using.
app.formula_tip: Drag a line like Linear: a pattern (Wave, Zigzag, Bounce or one you saved) swings the velocity up and down around it. Its settings show next to the tool buttons; changing them changes the line you just drew.
velocity_formula.pattern_tip: The pattern along the line. Your saved patterns (Formula → Pattern along the line → Custom…) are in the list too.
velocity_formula.loops_tip: How many times the pattern repeats between the line's two ends. Parts of a loop work too (4.5).
velocity_formula.number_tip: "{name}" in the pattern's formula, in velocity steps (a Wave of height 20 goes up to 20 above the line and 20 below it).
app.ctrl_flat_shift_snap_enter_done: Ctrl = flat · Shift = snap · Enter = done · select a shape to edit only its notes
app.a_ppq_of_or_more_many:
A PPQ of {PPQ_WARN} or more: many MIDI programs can't open the file.
Spiderweb still writes it.
app.128_the_standard_keys_0_127:
128: the standard keys 0–127, which every MIDI program reads.
256: keys 0–255, for players that support them (handy for tunings like 31edo).
Many MIDI programs can't read keys above 127, and playback here skips them.
app.builtin_settings_tip: Built-in BASSMIDI's settings: the soundfont, the voice limit, and lowering it by itself when the processor can't keep up.
app.voices_tip:
How many sounds Built-in BASSMIDI can ring at once (1000 to start). More = fuller in busy parts, but more work for the processor: if playback breaks up ("Overloaded" in red next to the Settings button), lower it.
Past the limit, the oldest sounds are cut.
bs.title: Built-in BASSMIDI settings
bs.change_tip: Pick another soundfont (.sf2 / .sfz). The Hz bass preview uses the same one.
bs.guard: Lower it by itself when overloaded
bs.guard_tip: Ticked: while the processor can't make the sound fast enough (it stops or crackles), the voice limit is lowered until it keeps up, then quickly raised back to yours once it's calm. Each Play starts from your limit (moving the play line while it plays keeps the lowered one).
bs.limiter_tip: Ticked: sound louder than full volume is turned down instead of clipped (clipping = a harsh, broken sound in busy parts), so busy parts sound cleaner but flatter. Off: too loud is clipped. Heard at once.
bs.limiter_slow: Without the optional speed-up Numba, playback may break up for a moment while you edit with it on.
app.pick_soundfont_title: Pick a soundfont for Built-in BASSMIDI
app.where_copied_and_pasted_notes_start:
Where copied and pasted notes start:
First note at tick 0: the first note lands right on the cursor / play line.
From the bar line: the empty space from the bar line before the first note
comes along, so the notes keep their place in the bar.
app.ctrl_shift_v_the_notes_copied:
Ctrl+Shift+V: the notes copied in Domino (Ctrl+C there) become one shape here.
It starts at the play line, like pasting in Domino (see the start setting above).
Every track's notes go into the one shape; controllers and other events are left out.
Ticks are taken as they are: use the same PPQ here.
app.ctrl_shift_c_copies_the_selected:
Ctrl+Shift+C: copies the selected shapes' notes (all notes when nothing is selected).
In Domino, paste with Ctrl+V at the cursor, or double-click a bar line in a track.
Multi channel: each channel goes into its own track, from that one down.
Ticks are copied as they are: use the same PPQ there.
app.glued: Glued touching notes: {before} notes → {after}. The shape remembers it: right-click → Remove glue takes it off
app.velocity_drawn_in_the_velocity_pane: Velocity drawn in the velocity pane. Typing a start/end here goes back to a straight ramp.
app.starts_exactly_on_the_last_point: starts exactly on the last point
app.too_many_points: Too many points to list ({n}): drag them on the piano roll.
app.ppq_must_be_a_whole_number: PPQ must be a whole number from 1 to 65535
app.bpm_must_be_a_number_at: BPM must be a number, at least 4
app.beats_per_bar_must_be_a: Beats per bar must be a whole number from 1 to 32
app.are_you_sure_you_want_to:
Are you sure you want to delete all {n} shapes?
(Ctrl+Z can bring them back.)
app.copied_shape_s_ctrl_v_pastes: Copied {n} shape(s) — Ctrl+V pastes them at the play line, a Select double-click on empty space where you click. Paste the text anywhere to share them
app.too_long: ({chars:,} characters: may be too long to paste in some places)
app.couldn_t_share: (couldn't put them on the clipboard as text to share: another program has it open)
app.shared_newer: This shared text was made by a newer Spiderweb. Update Spiderweb to paste it.
app.shared_broken: The shared text on the clipboard is cut off or changed, so it can't be pasted. Copy the whole line again.
app.shared_left_out: {n} of the shared shape(s) couldn't be read, so they were left out. They may have been made by a newer Spiderweb: update Spiderweb to paste them.
app.shared_made_short: (made by Spiderweb {version}: may look a little different)
app.clipboard_busy: Couldn't paste: another program has the clipboard open. Try again.

share.made_newer: This was made by a newer Spiderweb ({version}). Some things may have changed since, so it may look a little different than it did there. Updating Spiderweb makes sure it comes out right.
app.shared_drawing: The clipboard holds a shared drawing. Open the drawer and press Import to add it to your saved shapes.

big_ask.domino: This copies {n:,} notes: pasting that many can make the program you paste into slow.
big_ask.memory: It needs about {need} GB of memory ({free} GB free now).
big_ask.wont_fit: It needs about {need} GB of memory, but only {free} GB is free now: it will likely fail, or make this PC very slow. Closing other programs frees memory.

Copy anyway?

big_ask.out_of_memory: There wasn't enough memory to do this, so nothing was changed. Closing other programs frees memory.
big_ask.out_of_memory_somewhere: Spiderweb ran out of memory, so what you just did may not have finished. Undo (Ctrl+Z) takes it back. Closing other programs frees memory.
panel_custom.one_long_note_per_key_insid: One long note per key inside.
panel_custom.the_inside_filled_with_back: The inside filled with back-to-back notes of one gate.
panel_custom.just_the_outline_chopped_in: Just the outline, chopped into notes of one gate.
panel_custom.borders_tip: Where two areas of different colours meet (coloured in the drawer's Areas tool), the notes there go to the outline too. Off: the outline is only where the filled part ends.
panel_custom.too_many_colours: This shape needs {n} colours, but a shape can have at most {most} (the outline and the plain fill count too). The extra colours share the last one.
panel_custom.normal_all_its_notes_togeth:
Normal: all its notes together.
Outline: the notes along the edge of what's filled go on a channel of their own
and the inside's on another (the same gate, so they line up). Needs Channels: Multi channel.
panel_custom.channels_isn_t_multi_channe: Channels isn't Multi channel now, so it's all one channel (turns orange).
panel_custom.fill_and_spam_where_outline:
Fill and Spam: where outlines overlap, the overlap is left empty
(a shape inside a shape makes a hole). Off: everything the lines close in is filled,
overlaps and holes too, also where one line crosses itself.
panel_custom.each_key_s_notes_start_at:
Each key's notes start at that key's left edge,
so the left side is exact and the right side ragged.
panel_custom.every_note_sits_on_the_gate:
Every note sits on the gate grid counted from the start of the song,
so the notes form straight columns (lined up with bar lines and
other shapes); both sides are a little ragged.
panel_custom.centred_tip:
What doesn't fit a whole gate is shared between both ends of each key,
so a peak or a point comes out the same on both sides.
panel_custom.range_tip: Opens a window where the gate can go from one number to another across the shape (left to right, low to high or top to bottom), along a graph you can change. Every whole-tick gate in between gets an equal share, like a gate distribution: most notes get the short gates.
panel_custom.gate_ranged_tip: A gate Range is on: the gate goes from {a} to {b} ticks across the shape (Range… changes it). Changing this number takes the Range off, back to one gate for every note.
panel_custom.ends_tip:
What happens to the bit of each key that doesn't fit a whole gate.
Pictures of each: Help (F1) → Inside fill.
panel_custom.edge_tip:
Makes the outline at least this thick, so it doesn't get thin where the shape is steep. 0 = off.
It grows into the inside, so the shape's edge stays where it is. Where the shape is thinner than that, all of it becomes outline.
Works with Empty, Outline spam, and Fill / Spam set to "Outline". Lines that don't close have no inside and stay as they are.
panel_custom.edge_mode_tip:
Even band: the inside shrinks the same way on every side, top and bottom too, measured as the shape looked when it was first drawn (so a circle shrinks into a smaller circle), so the outline is equally thick all round, holes and inner corners included.
Grow sideways: each short outline note just grows longer toward the middle of its key.
colours.rows_tip:
From its start: each key row starts again at the first channel where its notes begin, so the colours follow the shape's left edge instead of making straight stripes.
From its end: each key row's last note gets the first channel, counting back, so the colours follow the shape's right edge (exact with Ends: Stretch or a short gate).
A row with a gap (like a ring's two sides) starts again after the gap too.
Spam and Outline spam shapes only.
colours.rows_only: None of the picked shapes is Spam or Outline spam: Fill, Empty and lines have one note per piece of a key row, so every note would start again (one colour).
colours.tip:
The notes take turns over several channels, so the colour changes with each turn (which colours you see depends on the program showing the MIDI).
By step: each step the next channel (spam: each gate column; lines: each note in time).
By key: each key the next channel (rows).
By time: a note length from the start of the song, like the snap (1/4 = a beat), so it lines up with the bar lines.
Channels: how many take turns. Every: how long one channel lasts.
Needs Channels: Multi channel.
colours.needs: Channels isn't Multi channel now: all its notes are in one channel, so the colour doesn't change.
panel_custom.hz_tip:
Spam so fast that the repeats sound like a tone.
The gate is worked out from the tone, the BPM and the PPQ, and gates of two sizes
(like 34 and 35 ticks) are mixed so the tone comes out exact. Every key is in step.
Best heard after the MIDI is rendered to an audio file.
panel_custom.hz_skipped: Some of the selected shapes are Hz bass. A Hz bass gets its gate from its tone, so it stays as it is: only the other shapes change.
panel_custom.hz_range_off: A gate Range doesn't work together with Hz bass, so it's switched off. Unticking Hz bass brings it back, with the gate it had.
panel_custom.hz_cents_tip: Pitch adjustment: 100 cents = one key up, -100 = one key down.
panel_custom.hz_short: The gates are short, so the tone wobbles: a higher PPQ fixes it.
panel_custom.hz_stale: The BPM changed since this Hz bass was made, so its tone is off now.
panel_custom.hz_gates_tip:
Auto: Fixed for a note that holds still when it's off by no more than the threshold,
else Alternating. A slide is always Alternating.
Alternating: gates of two sizes take turns, so the tone is exact.
Fixed: every gate is the same whole number of ticks, so the tone is a little off
(the higher the PPQ, the less).
hz.auto_tip:
Auto gates: a note that holds still gets Fixed gates when they're off
its tone by at most this many cents, else Alternating ones (0 to {most}).
About 5 cents is where most ears start to hear it.
Right-click a note to give it a threshold of its own.
hz.auto_shared: Use the Hz bass's threshold ({cents} cents)
hz.auto_ask:
Auto gates threshold of this note in cents, from 0 to {most}.
Fixed gates when they're off by at most this much, else Alternating.
With several selected, they all move by as much, each from its own value.
Drag the box sideways to try values.
hz.step_auto: Hz bass: a note's Auto threshold
hz.auto_fixed: Auto: Fixed gates (off by {off} cents, threshold {limit})
hz.auto_mixed: Auto: Alternating gates (Fixed would be off by {off} cents, threshold {limit})
hz.own_fixed: Fixed gates, this note's own (off by {off} cents)
hz.own_mixed: Alternating gates, this note's own (Fixed would be off by {off} cents)
panel_custom.hz_notes_tip:
Opens the Hz bass window: place notes there and the tone follows them.
Notes at the same time make a chord; the red line is the tone you really hear.
panel_custom.hz_short_fixed: The gates are short, so the tone is off: a higher PPQ fixes it.
panel_custom.hz_tool_info: Drag up or down on the piano roll where the Hz bass should start: that is the keys it repeats. Then place its notes in the window that opens.
hz.name: Hz bass
hz.grow_tip:
Ticked: the shape on the piano roll is made as long as the notes here.
Not ticked: the shape keeps its length, and notes past its end (the grey part) aren't used.
hz.pencil_tip:
Press on empty space to place a note. Ctrl+drag selects with a box.
Double right-click switches between Select and Pencil.
hz.select_tip:
Drag on empty space to select the notes the box touches (Ctrl: add to the selected ones; Shift: no snap).
Notes can still be moved and resized. Double right-click switches between Select and Pencil.
hz.ppq_tip:
The PPQ of the whole project (the same box as under Project).
A higher PPQ brings the red line closer to the exact tone.
hz.fx_tip:
Shows or hides the effects pane under the notes.
Effects that are on keep working while it's hidden.
hz.line_tip:
Ticked: the red line shows the tone you hear (the middle of a row = the exact tone).
The faint line behind it is each repeat's own pitch.
Zoomed in, drag it up or down to tune a note (double-click: back to 0). The dots of a slide can be dragged.
Not ticked: the line and its dots are hidden. Slides and tunes that were made stay.
hz.hint_none: Select a Hz bass to change its notes, or pick the Hz bass tool (H) and drag on the piano roll where a new one should start. To give a spam shape Hz bass notes, select it and press Notes… in the side panel.
hz.hint_new: New Hz bass starting at beat {beat}: click to place its first note.
hz.stale: BPM changed: this Hz bass is out of tune.
hz.undo_elsewhere: The last change was made on the piano roll: undo it there.
hz.redo_elsewhere: The next change to redo was made on the piano roll: redo it there.
hz.tune_ask:
Tune of this note in cents (100 = one key), from -{most} to {most}.
0 = the exact tone.
With several selected, they all move by as much, each from its own value.
Drag the box sideways to try values.
hz.fx_slant_tip: Slant: every key starts a little later than the key below it. 100 % = spread over one whole wave. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_groups_tip: Groups: the keys take turns in groups. 0 % = all together, 20 % = 2 groups, up to 6 groups at 100 %. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_offpitch_tip: Off pitch: every key repeats a little slower or faster than the tone, so the keys drift apart and meet again by themselves. 100 % = 2 % between the lowest and the highest key. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_noisy_tip: Noisy: every repeat is late by a random bit. 100 % = up to one whole wave. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_volume_tip: Volume: how loud. 100 % = the shape's own velocity, 0 % = silence (no notes there). Right-click → Repeat every + Shape → Pump for a pumping bass. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_sweep_tip: Sweep: a bump of loudness that travels over the keys. 0 % = the lowest keys are loud, 100 % = the highest. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_wah_tip: Wah: loud and quiet stripes over the keys, more stripes the higher the line (0 % = every key full). Strongest together with Slant. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_tremolo_tip: Tremolo: louder and quieter in turn. The line is how fast: 0 % = steady, 100 % = 8 times a beat (how much quieter: the synth window's Depth knob). Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_octave_tip: Octave below: every other repeat is softer, so the tone an octave below comes in. 100 % = as soft as it goes. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_vibrato_tip: Vibrato: the tone itself goes a little up and down, 5 times every two beats (or as the synth window's Rate knob says). 100 % = 5 % of its pitch each way. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_pitch_tip: Pitch: bends the tone up or down. 50 % = as placed, 100 % = 12 keys up, 0 % = 12 keys down. Points stick to whole keys (hold Shift for in between). With Repeat every: a wobble; Once per note: a drop or rise at each note. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_sine_tip: Sine: every key hits 16 times in each wave, loud then soft like a sine wave. It takes the overtones away: a soft, pure tone. 0 % = the plain tone. Many more notes. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_square_tip: Square: every key hits through half of each wave and rests through the other half. It takes every second overtone away: a hollow tone. 0 % = the plain tone. Many more notes. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_saw_tip: Saw: every key hits 16 times in each wave, softer and softer. It makes the high overtones a little quieter. 0 % = the plain tone. Many more notes. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_triangle_tip: Triangle: every key hits 16 times in each wave, louder, then softer. It takes every second overtone away and softens the rest. 0 % = the plain tone. Many more notes. Click it to put it on.
hz.fx_hint: Click an effect on the left to put it on: one line over all the notes. Drag its points, press on the line for a new point.
hz.fx_bend_tip: Drag up or down to bend this line. Double-click: straight again.
hz.fx_hold: Hold (a step at the next point)
hz.fx_sustain: Sustain here until the note ends

From the start of one bump to the start of the next, in ticks.

Smooth start and end: over this many ticks from each end of the range,
the bumps grow from nothing to full size (and shrink back to nothing at the end),

tumour_window.which_side_of_the_line_the: Which side of the line the bumps go (left / right as you go along the line from its start).

tumour_window.only_this_part_of_the_line: Only this part of the line gets bumps (0 % = its start, 100 % = its end).
tumour_window.fit_the_bumps_evenly_the_d:

the range exactly, with the last one landing right on its end.

pattern_dialog.shape_help:
t goes from 0 to 1 while the shape is drawn. The drawing is fitted to the curve: if it ends where it started (like a circle), it's as wide as from the curve's start A to its end B; if not, it starts at A and ends at B. It follows the curve, so bending the dotted curve bends the shape.
Works: numbers, t, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.
pattern_dialog.shape_edited_by_hand: Edited by hand. Its start and end points stay where they are (their handles can move).
pattern_dialog.whole_shape: The whole shape, between the curve's ends A and B. Drag a point to change it by hand; double-click the line to add a point, right-click a point to remove it. Alt + drag: a sharp corner. Wheel = zoom, drag empty space = move.
pattern_dialog.title: Pattern along the line
pattern_dialog.name: Name
pattern_dialog.along_tip: Can be left empty. Moves the line forward (+) or back (-) along the curve, in loops (1 = a whole loop). Where it goes back faster than the loop moves on, the line runs back over itself and makes curls.
pattern_dialog.sym_tip: Symmetric halves: only the first half of the formula counts. The second half is made from it, mirrored (like an arch) or turned half way round (like an S).
pattern_dialog.edit_formula_tip: Type your own formula. Any name in it other than x (like height) gets its own number box.
pattern_dialog.help:
One loop: x goes from 0 at its start to 1 at its end; y is how far to the side of the curve, in keys (up on a curve going to the right).
Works: numbers, x, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.
pattern_dialog.help_polygon:
One loop: x goes from 0 at its start to 1 at its end; y is how far to the side (outward), in hundredths of the polygon's height. Every side gets the pattern, and it grows and shrinks with the polygon.
Works: numbers, x, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.
pattern_dialog.help_drawer:
One loop: x goes from 0 at its start to 1 at its end; y is how far to the side of the curve, in hundredths of the board (100 = the whole board). The drawing keeps these sizes when it's placed, so they grow and shrink with it.
Works: numbers, x, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.
pattern_dialog.fit_view_tip: Show all of it again. Mouse wheel = zoom in and out; drag empty space (or middle-drag) = move around.
pattern_dialog.back_to_formula_tip: Forget the changes made by hand: the loop follows the formula again.

pattern_dialog.only_saved: Only your saved patterns can be deleted (the grey ones come with Spiderweb).
pattern_dialog.edited_by_hand: Edited by hand: every loop along the line follows this one.
pattern_dialog.one_loop: One loop, as long as it is on the curve. Drag a point to change it by hand; double-click the line to add a point, right-click a point to remove it. Alt + drag: a sharp corner. Wheel = zoom, drag empty space = move.

and a stroke that ends where it started becomes a perfect circle, ellipse, square, rectangle or triangle.
The higher, the simpler (a slightly oval loop: an ellipse, then a circle). The stroke as drawn is kept,
so you can change this any time. New freehand strokes use the last number picked.

help.about.title: About Spiderweb
help.about.tip: Version, license, and where Spiderweb keeps your files.
help.about.text: Free to use, share and change under the MIT License.
New versions, the source code and problem reports: {WEBSITE}

Spiderweb can look there for a new version by itself (set how often at the bottom of this page; Never turns it off). When there is one, a small window says what's new in it and has a button to open the download page. Nothing is downloaded by itself: to update, download the new Spiderweb.exe and put it in place of the old one. Your autosave and shapes stay.
All of the code was written by an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5, by Anthropic). Kanade Tachibana directed the project: decided what it should do, tested it and asked for changes.
Spiderweb's folder holds your autosave (and autosave-backup), your shape library (shapes), the MIDI files you generate (output) and errors.log, where the details go if something goes wrong.

help.welcome.title: Welcome to Spiderweb
help.welcome.tip: Draw lines and shapes on the piano roll and they become notes. Pick a tool at the top; a short tip like this one explains each the first time. F1 or the Help button: every tip, searchable.
help.welcome.text: Draw lines, curves and shapes on the piano roll; every key they cross gets notes, like drawing notes by hand but in one stroke.
1. Pick a tool at the top and draw. The arrow next to Line opens every drawing tool (Polyline, Freehand, Curve, Arc, Custom shape, Funnel, Text...); the pin next to one gives it its own button.
2. Select a shape to change it: drag its points, or change its settings in the panel on the right.
3. Space plays it. Right-drag listens to the notes under the mouse.
4. Set PPQ, BPM and the output file under Project, then Generate MIDI.
Your work is saved on its own (autosave) and comes back next time. Save… keeps a copy as a project file.
The first time you use a tool or feature, a small tip explains it. You can turn tips off or show them all again in this Help window (bottom).
help.whats_new.title: What's new
help.whats_new.tip: What changed in each version, newest first.
help.whats_new.text: What changed in each version, newest first. This page opens by itself the first time a new version starts.
Version 1.4.0

• Hz bass tool (H): spam so fast it sounds like a tone. Drag where it starts on the piano roll, then place notes in the window that opens (chords, slides). The red line there is the tone you really hear. Preview plays the Hz bass alone through a built-in synth with your soundfont.
• Hz bass effects: lines drawn under the notes change the sound over time (pitch, volume, vibrato, wah, tremolo and more). They can repeat, for example for a pumping bass.

• Select box: drag on empty space with Select to select what the box touches. Ctrl+drag adds another box. Drag a box's sides to stretch what it selected, the inside to move it, Ctrl+drag inside to move a copy. Right-click inside shows what works on all of them at once.
• With Select, double-click on empty space to paste there.

• Sharing shapes: Ctrl+C also copies the shapes as one line of text. Paste it anywhere to share it; others paste it into their Spiderweb with Ctrl+V. In the drawer, Export and Import do the same for drawings (Import adds them to your shape library).
• Scrollbars on the piano roll: drag the bar to scroll, drag one of its ends to zoom, or use the − / + buttons.

• Coloured areas: in the drawer, the new Areas tool (B) gives each piece of a custom shape a colour of its own, or leaves it empty. Click an area or drag across several; "Reset all colours" puts them all back. A line under the colours counts them (a shape has at most 15). On the piano roll they count with Fill or Spam and Multi channel.
• Stroke roles (right-click a stroke): Outline and fill (normal), Outline only (notes on top of the fill, cuts no hole), or Fill line (no notes, just splits the inside into areas to colour).

• Outline colour (right-click a stroke): the stroke's notes in a colour of their own. "Outline between colours" (under Fill and Spam, with Outline on) puts the notes where two colours meet on the outline too.
• Colours (side panel, under Velocity): any shape's notes take turns over several channels by step, key or time, so the colour keeps changing.
• Smoother with lots of notes: moving the view and dragging shapes.

• New pattern: Curls (right-click a line → Formula → Pattern along the line). The line loops back over itself in little curls; "curl" sets how tight they are. In Custom…, the new "along =" formula moves a pattern forward or back along the line.

• Formulas on more lines: polylines have them now, and so do the strokes of a live shape on the piano roll and the drawer's lines, polylines and arcs (right-click the stroke → Formula). Turn into live shape (Ctrl+L) keeps them.

• Strum: select shapes, right-click → Strum… (Alt+S). The notes of each chord start one after another, like strumming a guitar, so a straight edge of notes becomes a slope or a curve. It works like the strum tool of other piano rolls (Time, Velocity, Tension, Preserve end, Trigger ahead, End, Chop chords, Alternate direction), and every knob shows its real value, which you can type past where the knob reaches. The shape remembers its strum.
• Claw machine: no longer beta. Its shortcut is now Alt+W (was Ctrl+K).

• Outline gate (side panel, with Empty, Outline spam or Outline on): makes the outline at least so many ticks thick, so it doesn't get thin where the shape is steep. It grows into the inside, so the shape's edge stays where it is.
• The tumour window works like the Claw machine and Strum windows: changes show at once, Accept keeps them (one undo step), X or Esc puts the lines back, and Reset puts every setting back.
• Selected shapes keep their own colours: a thin red line goes round their notes instead.
• The side panel only shows the settings that do something for what's picked.
• Join, Split and Turn into live shape left the Shapes box: they're in the right-click menu and on Ctrl+G, Ctrl+Shift+G and Ctrl+L.
Version 1.3.0

• Polygon tool (Q), next to Circle, instead of Square and Triangle: pick how many points it has and its kind in the panel (polygon, star, or crossing star). Its sides can have a shape or a pattern (right-click → Formula).

• Claw machine: select shapes, right-click → Claw machine… (Alt+W). It cuts slices of time out of the notes, or keeps some notes and trashes some (by notes, keys, chords or at random), and can shorten notes instead of removing them. The shape remembers its claw, so moving or reshaping it keeps it.

• Formulas: right-click a curve, line or arc → Formula. "Shape of the line" makes it a circle, spiral, flower, heart, figure 8, slow or fast start, or S-curve. "Pattern along the line" lays a wave, zigzag, bounce, square wave, sawtooth, teeth, spikes, half circles, stair steps, swell or fading wave along it. Custom… makes your own, with a preview you can zoom and move. Drawer curves, funnel curves and polygon sides have them too. "Turn into plain curve" makes the result an ordinary curve.
• Symmetric halves (Off / Mirrored / Turned) for formula shapes and patterns: the first half makes the second. Shapes changed by hand or turned into a plain curve stay symmetric.
• Velocity pane: a Formula tool (a line with a wave, zigzag, bounce or saved pattern swinging around it).

• Update check: Spiderweb can look for a new version when it starts (every time, once a day, week or month, or never) and show what's new in it. Set it in Help → About; "Check now" looks right away. Nothing is downloaded by itself.
• This What's new page.
• Undo and Redo buttons on the toolbar (between Fit view and Play).
• Funnel: lines on both sides of the wall make two halves, each with its own notes running to the wall. Notes ending on the wall make the same steps as notes starting on it.
• Paste from Domino with Multi channel: every copied track gets a channel of its own.
• Easier picking of lines, strokes, funnel parts and a box's corners and sides. Clicking the faint dashed line under a formula curve selects the shape.
• Steep lines give 1-tick notes to keys that share a tick.
• The Custom… formula window and the tumour graph have their own undo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y). The graph has From / to boxes and a right-click menu on its points.
• Curves fitted from drawn paths follow long, wiggly paths with fewer anchors, and sharp corners stay sharp.
Version 1.2.0
• Inside fill: Spam ends (round, keep, drop, no slivers, stretch), Normal / Outline, Overlaps cancel out, and outlines with gaps can be filled.
• Turn into live shape (Ctrl+L): lines, curves and arcs become one custom shape that can be filled.
• Tumours: their own window, Rotation and Slant, and graphs so the numbers can change along the line.
• Join (Ctrl+G) and Split (Ctrl+Shift+G), and Split here on a line's right-click menu.
• Snap: the usual list of note lengths with note pictures, plus Custom….
• History panel, Keys 128 / 256, picking shapes by their notes, Paste from Domino can start at the bar line, more tips, and typing anywhere in Help searches.
Version 1.1.0
• Copy to Domino (Ctrl+Shift+C) and Paste from Domino (Ctrl+Shift+V).
Version 1.0.0
• The first version.

help.select.title: Select (V)
help.select.tip: Click a shape to select it, drag it to move, drag its squares to reshape. Drag empty space = select with a box, click empty space = move the play line. Double right-click = to the last drawing tool and back.
help.select.text: Click a shape (its line or one of its notes) to select it (where shapes overlap: a line first, then the one on top; a selected shape under the mouse stays the one you drag); Ctrl+click selects more (Ctrl+A = all). Drag a shape to move it (all selected ones move together), drag its squares to reshape it.
Drag on empty space to draw a box: it selects every shape it touches (its line or one of its notes). Ctrl+drag adds them to the ones selected. Click empty space (no drag) to move the play line there.

Right-click a shape (or one of its notes) = its menu (delete, duplicate, copy, flip, turn, add a point…). Right-click empty space = deselect. Double right-click switches between Select and the last drawing tool.
Blue curve handles can be dragged with any tool.
help.select.words: move pick choose drag box rectangle marquee area double right-click switch toggle last tool
help.line.title: Line (L)
help.line.tip: Drag from start to end, or click the start and then click the end.
help.line.text: Drag from the start to the end, or click the start and click the end (the line follows the mouse in between; right-click or Esc cancels).
Each key the line crosses gets one note, starting where the line reaches that key, so a slope becomes a smooth staircase. Points snap to the grid (Snap at the top); hold Shift to place them freely.
Last note (panel): the last note ends on the line's end, or starts exactly on it.
Right-click it: Formula (a shape or a pattern along it, see Formulas).
help.poly.title: Polyline (P)
help.poly.tip: Click point after point (or drag each piece). Double-click or right-click to finish.
help.poly.text: Click point after point, or drag each piece. Double-click, right-click or Enter finishes it; Esc cancels.
Selected polyline: drag its squares to move points; middle-click on it adds a point where it fits best.
Last note (panel) works at every point: each piece is its own line.
Right-click it: Formula (a shape or a pattern along it, see Formulas).
help.free.title: Freehand (F)
help.free.tip: Drag to draw. Straighten (panel) turns it into perfect lines, curves or shapes.
help.free.text: Hold the mouse button and draw.

Straighten (panel, 0-100) makes it perfect: 0 = as you drew it, higher = straighter lines and smoother curves. A stroke that ends where it started becomes a perfect circle, ellipse, square, rectangle or triangle. The higher, the simpler (a slightly oval loop becomes an ellipse, then a circle). The stroke as drawn is kept, so change it any time. New strokes use the last number you picked.
help.free.words: draw hand pencil smooth straighten shape recognition
help.curve.title: Curve (C)
help.curve.tip: Drag from start to end (or click both), then bend it with its blue handles. Middle-click the curve to add an anchor.
help.curve.text: Drag from the start to the end, or click both. Then shape it (see Curves: anchors and handles): drag the blue dots to bend it, middle-click the curve to add an anchor.
Right-click it: Formula (a shape like a spiral or heart, a pattern like a wave along it: see Formulas), Symmetric halves (one half follows the other), add an anchor, and the usual menu.
help.arc.title: Arc (A)
help.arc.tip: Click the start, a point it passes through, and the end. Or drag from start to end, then move the mouse to bend it and click.
help.arc.text: A piece of a perfect circle. Click its start, a point it passes through, then its end. Or drag from the start to the end, then move the mouse to bend it and click.
It's round as the piano roll looks while you draw it. Put the end on the start for a whole circle.
Selected: drag its round middle point (any tool) to bend it, its squares to move the ends. Right-click it: Formula (a shape or a pattern along it, see Formulas).
help.custom.title: Custom shape (S)
help.custom.tip: Pick a shape in the panel (or make one with Drawer…), then drag a box to place it.
help.custom.text: Pick a shape in the panel, or draw your own with Drawer…. Then drag a box on the piano roll (or click two corners); the drawing stretches to fill it. Ctrl keeps its drawn proportions.
Its inside can be filled (see Inside fill). Circle and Polygon (O / Q), in the drawing tools' list (the arrow next to Line), make that shape straight away (Ctrl = perfect, as it looks).
A placed shape keeps its own copy: changing the library shape later doesn't change it.
help.box.title: Circle and Polygon (O / Q)
help.box.tip: Drag a box (or click two corners). Ctrl = a perfect circle or polygon as it looks. Polygon: pick the points and kind (polygon, star, crossing star) in the panel.
help.box.text: Drag a box on the piano roll, or click two corners. Ctrl makes it perfect as it looks on screen (a circle, a square, an equal-sided triangle or star).

Polygon: the panel sets how many Points it has (3 = triangle, 4 = square, 5 = pentagon…) and its Kind. Polygon has a flat side at the bottom. Star: outer and inner points take turns; Inner size is how far out the inner points are, in % of the outer ones (100 = a polygon with twice the points). Crossing star: joins every Skip-th point with straight lines that cross, like a pentagram (5 points, skip 2); when the two share a divisor it's several loops (6 points, skip 2 = two triangles). Change them any time with the polygon selected; the panel's numbers are also used for the next one you draw.

The sides can have a shape: right-click the polygon → Formula → Shape of the line (Quarter circle, S-curve, your own…). Every side becomes that shape, from its corner to the next one, so a square can become a flower of arches. A closed shape (like Circle) sits on each side as wide as the side, and the sides stay straight.

The sides can also have a pattern: right-click the polygon → Formula → Pattern along the line (a wave, zigzag, spikes, your own…). Every side gets the same pattern: Each piece gives every side all the loops, Across all runs them on round the whole outline. Its height is in hundredths of the polygon's height, so it grows with the shape. Symmetric halves work on it too. "Turn into plain lines" makes the result plain lines (the polygon settings go).

They're custom shapes, so their inside can be filled (see Inside fill) and they resize, turn and skew like any custom shape (see Custom shapes: resize, turn, skew). With Live shape on they're drawn into the live shape instead.

help.funnel.title: Funnel (N)
help.funnel.tip: Draw its line, then its wall (drag, or click twice each). Then middle-click on the line to start a curve there.
help.funnel.text: Draw the funnel's line, then its wall (drag each, or click twice). Either can come first; a wall earlier in time than the line's start makes a reverse funnel. Ctrl while drawing or dragging the wall keeps it centred on the line.

Middle-click on the line (any tool) to start a curve there: curves go to both ends of the wall. Middle-click near a curve to add an anchor it goes through. The curves have anchors and handles (see Funnel curves).

With a funnel selected, a line drawn to (or from) its wall is added to it (two-line funnels). Lines on the other side of the wall make their own half, with its own notes running to the wall: they just start (or end) on the wall; the wall setting is for the first line's side.
Panel: the wall (notes end on it, or start on it), the inside (spam or long notes) and the gate. Tick "Different start and wall gate" to let the gate change from the start to the wall.
help.text.title: Text (X)
help.text.tip: Click on the piano roll and type. Esc = done. The letters become a custom shape.
help.text.text: Click on the piano roll and type (Enter = new line, Esc = done). The letters become a custom shape, so they can be filled, moved, resized, turned and skewed.
Panel: font, size (font size, or rows = how many keys capital letters are), weight and italic, plus:
Letter spacing: extra room between the letters, in 1/1000 of the font size. Minus numbers pull them closer together.
Line spacing: room between lines (Enter starts a new line), in % of the font's own line spacing.
Align: where the text sits on the spot you clicked. Left = it starts there, Centre = its middle is there, Right = it ends there. With several lines it also lines them up.
Text is a custom shape, so Empty, Fill, Spam and Outline spam work on its letters too (see Inside fill).
Threshold (Fill / Spam): how much of a key's height has to be inside a letter for that key to play there. 50% = the key's middle. Lower = chunkier letters, higher = thinner.
Grow: makes the letters' strokes thicker, in keys (minus = thinner). Big values can look odd in tight corners.
Click a text with the Text tool (or double-click it with Select) to retype it. Drag, Shift+arrows, double-click (a word) or Ctrl+A select letters; Ctrl+C / X / V copy, cut and paste them.
help.hz_bass.title: Hz bass (H)
help.hz_bass.tip: Drag up or down on the piano roll where it starts (the keys it repeats), then place notes in the window that opens: spam so fast it sounds like those tones. The red line there is the tone you really hear.
help.hz_bass.text: Spam so fast that the repeats sound like a tone. It is best heard after the MIDI is rendered to an audio file; the Preview button in its window gives a quick idea of it without leaving Spiderweb.

Drag up or down on the piano roll where it should start: the red mark shows the keys it will repeat (more keys = a thicker tone, not a different one). You can also click, move the mouse and click again.

A window opens with a small piano roll of its own: the notes you place there are the tones you will hear, and the Hz bass on the main piano roll grows as you place them. Notes at the same time make a chord. Empty space between notes is silence.
To change the keys it repeats later, drag the top or bottom side of its box on the main piano roll.

With short gates the tone wobbles (Alternating) or is off (Fixed): an orange line in the panel says so. A higher PPQ fixes it. After the BPM changes, the tone is off: an orange line says so, and Update Hz bass makes it right again.

Any custom shape with Spam or Outline spam can have Hz bass too: tick Hz bass in the panel for one tone, or press Notes… to place notes for it. The shape keeps its length (notes past its end aren't used) unless Shape length follows the notes is ticked in the window.
The rest is in the Hz bass section of this Help: placing notes, the tone, slides, the preview, effects and the synth window.
help.picture.title: Image (I)
help.picture.tip: Turns an image (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP...) into notes in up to 15 colours. Set it up in the window that opens, then drag it into the piano roll.
help.picture.text: The Image tool opens the image window. Open an image there (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, BMP or TIFF), set it up, then drag the handle at the bottom right into the piano roll (you hold the image by its middle; its start snaps to the grid, hold Shift to place it exactly) or press "Place at the play line". A placed image always stays inside the piano roll's keys.

Made for: Falling notes = the keys run across the image (players with the keyboard at the bottom). Piano roll = the keys run up the image (players and editors with the keys on the left). An image shows the right way up in one of them only. Piano roll gives a wide image about three times the detail, because the keys go along its short side.
Hold the mouse button on the preview, or hold Space, to see the original image in its place.
Every slider is only a suggestion: try them and judge by eye. Double-click a slider to put it back to its suggested value; "Back to suggested" puts them all back.

Size: Keys = how many keys tall (or wide) the image is. Steps per key = how much finer than a key the image is the other way (time costs nothing, so more steps = more detail). One step = how long one step lasts: more ticks = a taller image in the player.

A big image is made with a progress bar on the preview: press Cancel there (or Esc) to stop it (the image and its settings go back to how they were). Past a million grid cells (up to that many notes) you're asked first.

Colours: an image has at most 15 colours, one per channel (channel 10 is left out). Click a colour to pick it yourself; it stays as picked (a corner mark). Right-click it to let Spiderweb pick it again. Focus on: whole = every part of the image counts the same; details = faces, eyes and edges get their colours first.

Blending mixes neighbouring colours so the eye sees colours in between. Spread is the closest to the original; Keep details stops it from washing away small things like a mouth or eyes. Pattern is a fixed even pattern. None = only the nearest colour.

Player look (second tab) only changes the preview, so it matches the player you use: flat notes, or notes with a dark outline and shading. "Join same-colour notes into one" changes the notes too: on = fewer, longer notes.

The outline's px are your player's: how thick it looks depends on the player's window size. Type your player's window size and how many keys it shows (Player window, Keys shown), and the preview draws the outline as thick as it would look there.

The colours you see are what each channel should look like in the player: a MIDI file has no colours, only channels. The notes on the piano roll keep their channels: colour 1 = channel 1, and so on, whatever the Channels setting is. Any other shape on the same channel takes that colour in the player too.

Colour list for the player (Player look tab): Copy colours puts the colours on the clipboard as text for your player's settings, in the format picked. "Colour by" Channel numbers them by channel (a player that colours by channel); "in order" numbers them 1, 2, 3 (a player that colours tracks in order). "What Copy gives" shows the exact text. Edit formats... opens the format editor: Start, Each colour and End boxes, tags to click in, and the text it gives as you type. Built-in formats can't change: editing one makes your own copy.

Paste colours... reads colours out of any text (a whole player settings file is fine): pick the list you want, then lock the colours (the image uses exactly them) or use them only as a starting point.
Use channel 10: 16 colours, colour 10 on channel 10. Many players draw channel 10's notes, but they play no sound (or drums). Shapes never use channel 10.
Several images in one project share one set of colours (a player has only one). Share sets how much this image counts when they compete for colours.

Resizing a placed image makes its notes again from the image file, so it stays sharp. If the file is gone, the image still plays as it is (stretched), and the image window offers to find the file. If the file changed since it was placed, you're asked whether to use the new version. Keep images in your project's folder: they're saved relative to it, so both can move together.

help.hz_notes.title: Placing notes (Hz bass)
help.hz_notes.tip: In the Hz bass window, press the mouse to place a note and drag it; drag either end to change its length. Select (V) draws a box around notes.
help.hz_notes.text: In the Hz bass window, pressing the mouse places a note at once, and it follows the mouse until you let go. A note that is there moves the same way; drag either end to change its length. A new note is as long as the last one you clicked or resized. While you hold a note, its key sounds on the MIDI-out device.

Select (V) and Pencil (P) are at the top of the window; double right-click switches between the two. With Select, dragging on empty space draws a box that selects the notes it touches (Ctrl adds them); with Pencil, Ctrl+drag does it. The box snaps to the grid like on the piano roll.
Drag the box's right side to make all its notes longer or shorter by the same amount (they keep their starts), or drag inside it to move them.
Ctrl+click picks several, Ctrl+A all; Delete removes the selected notes.

Ctrl+C copies the selected notes and Ctrl+V pastes them at the play line (the preview's, or the main window's when the preview is off); with Select, double-click empty space to paste them there. With the preview on, a click on empty space with Select moves the play line there.
The window has its own Snap (Shift = no snap). The mouse wheel scrolls, Shift+wheel goes sideways, Ctrl+wheel zooms, the middle button drags the view.

help.hz_tone.title: Tone and tuning (Hz bass)
help.hz_tone.tip: The red line is the tone you hear. Zoomed in, drag it in a note to tune that note. Gates: Alternating = exact, Fixed = a little off.
help.hz_tone.text: The red line is the tone you hear; the middle of a row is the exact tone (a green line when you zoom in).

Every repeat lasts a whole number of ticks, so each one is a little off, more at a low PPQ: the faint line behind the red one shows every repeat's own pitch. With Alternating gates the repeats take turns being too high and too low (the faint line jumps) and the average, the red line, is exact. With Fixed gates every repeat is off the same way, so the red line itself sits off to one side.

Zoomed in, drag the red line in a note up or down to tune that note alone (whole cents, Shift = finer; it sticks to the exact tone). Double-click the red line to put the tune back to 0. Right-click a note and pick Tune… to type it.

In the window's toolbar: Pitch moves every tone in cents (100 = one key). Gates: Alternating = gates of two sizes take turns so the tone is exact; Fixed = every gate is a whole number of ticks, a little off.

Auto gates (what a new Hz bass starts with): a note that holds still gets Fixed gates when they're off its tone by no more than the threshold (the number next to Gates, in cents), else Alternating ones. A slide is always Alternating.

In the window a band around each note's tone shows the threshold: green = Fixed, orange = Alternating. Hold the mouse over a note to see how far off Fixed gates would be. Right-click a note and pick Own Auto threshold… to give it (and the other selected notes) a threshold of its own. About 5 cents is where most ears start to hear it; the highest is 50 (half a key).

help.hz_slides.title: Slides (Hz bass)
help.hz_slides.tip: To make the tone slide from one note to another: select both, right-click → Slide between the selected notes. Or middle-click one note, then the other.
help.hz_slides.text: The line stops at the end of each note, and the tone jumps at the next note. To make it slide instead, select two notes (the second one starting at or after the end of the first), right-click and pick Slide between the selected notes; or middle-click a note where the slide should start and another note where it should end.
Two dots show: drag them to change the slide. Middle-click a dot to remove the slide.
A slide belongs to its two notes: notes added later don't change it.

A note can slide to several notes and several notes can slide to one: select the one note and the others (three or more notes) and pick Slide between the selected notes, or middle-click for each slide.

help.hz_preview.title: Preview (Hz bass)
help.hz_preview.tip: Preview plays this Hz bass alone through Spiderweb's own synth with your soundfont. Grey over the notes = not made yet.
help.hz_preview.text: Preview (at the top of the Hz bass window) lets you hear this Hz bass alone, through a synth built into Spiderweb, with a soundfont of yours: no MIDI-out device is needed. The first time, it asks for a soundfont (.sf2 or .sfz). It's a quick guide, not a final render: another program will sound a bit different.

The sound is made ahead of time, about a minute ahead of the play line (or of the left edge of the view when nothing plays). What isn't made yet is greyed over the notes, and clears as it's made. Change a note and only that stretch goes grey again.
Space plays and stops; click the bar numbers to move the play line (blue). If playing catches up with the grey, it waits there instead of skipping notes.

Preview settings… opens a small window: pick another soundfont, set the voice limit (how many sounds can ring at once: more is fuller but slower to make), leave out the soundfont's reverb and chorus, and set the volume.

It also shows how many voices are in use (orange when the limit is reached: the oldest sounds are cut short) and how fast the sound is made (orange when it's slower than playing). Change the voice limit and the notes grey again while it's made anew, so you hear the difference at once. A limiter always keeps the sound from getting too loud.

help.hz_effects.title: Effects (Hz bass)
help.hz_effects.tip: Effects are lines in the pane under the notes: click an effect's name to put it on, then drag its points.
help.hz_effects.text: Effects, in the pane under the notes, change how the tone sounds (only Pitch and Vibrato move its pitch). Click an effect's name on the left to put it on. Hold the mouse over a name to see what it does, at the bottom of the window.
Each effect is one line over all the notes, in step with them: 0 % at the bottom, 100 % at the top, flat before its first point and after its last.

Drag a point to move it, press on the line to add a point, double-click a point to delete it (deleting the last one takes the effect off; Delete with no points selected takes the highlighted effect off).
Drag the small round handle in the middle of a line up or down to bend it (double-click it: straight again); right-click a line → Hold makes it a step. Right-click for more.

Click a name that's on to highlight its line (the others go faint); click it again to see them all. While one effect is highlighted, pressing on another's faint line adds a point to the highlighted one.
The small square before a name that's on switches the effect off and on again without losing its line (Bypass).

To select several points, drag a box around them with Select (or Ctrl+drag with either tool): drag one of them to move them all, Delete deletes them, Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V copy them and paste them where the mouse is (into the highlighted effect, if any).
With the Pencil tool and an effect highlighted, drag on empty space to draw its line: with snap on it draws a step in every grid cell, with Shift (or snap off) a smooth line.
Lines that move sound more alive than flat ones. Very fast movement is hard to hear.

An effect can repeat, like an automation that repeats every beat: right-click it → Repeat every…, and type how long one repeat is as a note length, like the snap (1 / 4 = one beat); green lines show where each repeat starts while you type. The line you drew is squeezed into one repeat, and that repeat plays over and over from the start of the Hz bass. Change any copy and they all change.

Right-click → Shape gives a ready-made one (sine, triangle, saw, square, pump, random steps). Stop repeating stretches it back over the notes. Right-click → Amount line adds a dotted line over the notes that says how strong the repeat is (0 % = as if the effect were off), for example to fade a pump in.

help.hz_envelope.title: Once per note and sustain (Hz bass)
help.hz_envelope.tip: An effect can start over at every note, like a synth's envelope, and wait at a sustain point until the note ends.
help.hz_envelope.text: An effect can also start at each note, like an envelope: in the Repeat every… window, set Plays to Once per note. Its line then plays once from the start of every note, for as long as Lasts says, and stays on its last value until the note ends.
Restart at each note repeats it but starts it over at every note. Tick Stretch to each note to make it last as long as each note instead.
Each note has its own, as in a synth: a note added on top of another starts its effects over alone. A note reached by a slide carries on, it doesn't start again.
Right-click → Shape → Drop, Rise or Pluck gives a ready-made one (pitch: falls from 12 keys up, rises from 12 keys down, or a quick bump up).

Changes faster than about half a beat at 120 BPM are hard to hear: the tone only changes once per wave. Volume sounds about the same in its top half (renders often hit their limiter), so a fade is heard mostly near 0 %.

A line that plays once per note can have a sustain point, like a synth's envelope: right-click one of its points → Sustain here until the note ends (it turns into a diamond). The line plays up to that point, stays there for as long as the note lasts, and the rest of it (the fall) plays after the note ends.
The note keeps sounding during the fall, even under the notes after it (both sound there, like a chord), unless a note of the same tone starts. A slide doesn't end the note.
A note that ends before reaching the sustain point falls from wherever it got to. The dashed lines show where each fall starts.

help.hz_effect_list.title: Every effect (Hz bass)
help.hz_effect_list.tip: What each Hz bass effect does, one line each.
help.hz_effect_list.text: Slant: every key starts a little later than the key below it.
Groups: the keys take turns in groups (20 % = 2 groups, up to 6).
Off pitch: every key repeats a little faster or slower, so the keys drift apart and meet again.
Noisy: every repeat is late by a random bit.
Vibrato: the tone goes a little up and down.
Pitch: bends the tone up or down, up to 12 keys each way (points stick to whole keys; Shift = in between).
Volume: how loud (0 % = silence, no notes there).
Sweep: a bump of loudness travels over the keys.
Wah: loud and quiet stripes over the keys (strongest together with Slant).
Tremolo: louder and quieter in turn (the line is how fast).
Octave below: every other repeat is softer, so the tone an octave below comes in.

Sine, Square, Saw, Triangle: every key hits 16 times in each wave, loud and soft in the shape of that wave. Sine takes the overtones away (a soft, pure tone), Square and Triangle take every second one away (a hollow tone), Saw makes the high ones a little quieter. 0 % is the plain tone.
The waveforms make many more notes, up to 16 times as many: the count is at the bottom of the window.

help.live.title: Live shape (G)
help.live.tip: Lines, curves, arcs, freehand and boxes you draw now go into ONE custom shape. Close its outline to fill it. Right-click empty space to start the next one.
help.live.text: With Live shape on, Line, Polyline, Freehand, Curve, Arc, Circle and Polygon draw into one custom shape (the selected one, or a new one) instead of making separate shapes. Outlines that meet end to end join up, so a closed drawing can be filled (see Inside fill). Points snap onto the drawing's ends; clicking a polyline's first point closes it; letting go of a freehand stroke near its start closes it. Right-click empty space (deselect) to start the next shape.
While it's on, the selected shape's points show (purple squares): drag them with Select. Points in the same spot move together, and a point dropped on another one joins it.

Select tool: click a stroke of the selected shape to pick it: Del deletes it, a curve shows its handles, a freehand stroke can be straightened. Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V, Ctrl+H / Ctrl+J and Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right copy, paste, flip and turn just that stroke (Esc unpicks it: then they work on the whole shape again). A copied stroke is pasted into the selected custom shape, a grid step later and a key lower each time (nothing selected: into a new shape). Right-click a stroke = its menu, also: Formula for a line, polyline, arc or curve stroke (see Formulas), and save the drawing to the shape library. Its "This stroke" part sets the stroke's role and outline colour, like the drawer's (see Drawer: Select and editing).
help.turn_live.title: Turn into live shape (Ctrl+R)
help.turn_live.tip: Select lines, curves, arcs (or custom shapes) and press Ctrl+R: they become one live shape, so they can be filled. Split into separate shapes (Ctrl+Shift+G) gives them back.
help.turn_live.text: Lines can't be filled, custom shapes can. Select one or more lines, polylines, freehand strokes, curves or arcs (custom shapes too) and press Ctrl+R, or right-click one → Turn into live shape. They become one live shape (a custom shape) with each of them as a stroke of its own kind: curves stay curves with their anchors, arcs stay arcs, a straightened freehand stroke stays straightened, formulas stay on (a joined curve's become a plain curve). Then Fill, Spam and Outline spam work (see Inside fill), and its strokes can be edited like any live shape's.

The notes stay the same, and so do the velocities (where shapes play at the same time, the first selected one's win). With Multi channel each stroke still remembers the shape it came from, so strokes that clash still get channels of their own; the shape list says how many channels a shape uses (orange above 15).
What changes (Spiderweb asks first when it applies): tumours become fixed points, and "Last note: starts on it" is dropped.

Going back: Split into separate shapes (Ctrl+Shift+G, or right-click → Split back into the old shapes) gives the old shapes back exactly as they were, tumours and all, as long as the drawing wasn't changed (moving the whole shape is fine; resizing, turning, flipping or editing its strokes isn't: then it splits into groups of touching strokes instead). Ctrl+Z always works.

help.fill.title: Inside fill (custom shapes)
help.fill.tip: Empty = just the outline. Fill = one long note per key inside. Spam = back-to-back notes of the gate. Outline spam = the outline chopped into notes of the gate. Ends = what to do with the bit that doesn't fit a whole gate. Outline (box next to Fill / Spam) = the edge on its own channel.
help.fill.text: How a custom shape (and text) is filled, in the panel:
Empty: just the outline, like lines (upright parts get 1-tick notes).
Fill: one note per stretch of each key inside.

Spam: back-to-back notes of the gate. Start: Auto = each key from its own left edge; Aligned = on the gate grid from the song's start (straight columns); Centred = what doesn't fit a whole gate is shared between both ends (peaks come out the same on both sides).

Ends: with a gate of 1 tick every key is filled exactly. With a longer gate, a key's stretch is rarely a whole number of gates, so something has to give at its ends: Ends picks what happens to the bit that doesn't fit a whole gate. The same goes for Outline spam. The pictures show the same triangle each time.
Round to a gate (new shapes start with this one): a whole gate if it's at least half a gate, else dropped. Every key gets at least one gate, so the edge stays in whole gates.
Start: Auto
[clip:fill-ends-round]
Start: Centred
[clip:fill-ends-round-centred]
Keep leftovers: kept as a shorter note, so the edge follows the outline exactly.
Start: Auto
[clip:fill-ends-keep]
Start: Centred
[clip:fill-ends-keep-centred]
Drop leftovers: dropped. A key too short for even one gate still gets one shorter note, so points end in thin slivers.
Start: Auto
[clip:fill-ends-drop]
Start: Centred
[clip:fill-ends-drop-centred]
No slivers: like Drop leftovers, but no note shorter than a quarter gate.
Start: Auto
[clip:fill-ends-min]
Start: Centred
[clip:fill-ends-min-centred]
Stretch gates: each key's gates are stretched or squeezed a little so a whole number fits exactly. Start doesn't matter then, so there's one picture.
[clip:fill-ends-stretch]
Outline spam: the outline chopped into notes of the gate.

Range… (next to the gate, Spam and Outline spam) opens a window where the gate goes from one number to a second one across the shape instead of being the same everywhere. Opening it turns the Range on; untick "Use a gate range" there to take it off. From is the shape's gate, to is the second gate, and the graph sets how it gets there: the straight line gives every whole-tick gate between the two an equal share, like a gate distribution, so most notes get the short gates. Left to right (time): every key is cut at the same places, starting at the shape's left edge; with "Each key row by itself" every row instead runs the whole range along its own length (each piece of a row on its own, or across the gaps with "Across gaps in a row"), and a row too short for any note gets one note of the first gate. Low to high or Top to bottom (keys): each key gets its own gate. "Fit to the shape's edges" stretches or trims each row's first and last note so the notes reach exactly to the shape's edges, with no blank and nothing sticking out. Beside the graph, "Notes per gate" shows how many notes get each gate (red: a gate no note gets; point at a bar for its numbers). Start and Ends don't apply then. While a Range is on, the gate box in the side panel is orange; typing a new gate there takes the Range off.

Hz bass (Spam and Outline spam): spam so fast that the repeats sound like a tone. Tick it and type the key whose tone you want (like A1); the gate is worked out from that tone, the BPM and the PPQ. Every key is in step, so more keys make the tone thicker, not different. Notes… opens a window to place several tones, chords and slides (see Hz bass).

Gaps: where the outline isn't closed (red dots in the drawer), Fill and Spam close it with straight lines, shown dashed, and the buttons turn orange. Loose ends that nearly touch (within 1/64 beat and 1 key) are joined to each other first; every open part left is closed from its end back to its start. An open part that's almost straight (never more than half a key or 1/64 beat from that closing line) has nothing inside, so it isn't filled: it just keeps its notes. Close the gaps yourself to decide exactly where the edge goes.
[clip:fill-gap]

A line whose ends both land on a line (another one, or partway along itself) isn't a gap. It splits the area it crosses: both sides stay as they were (filled or empty), and the line keeps its own notes.

Normal / Outline (the box next to Fill and Spam): Outline puts the notes along the edge of what's filled on a channel of their own (with Overlaps cancel out ticked that's every edge, around every filled bit; unticked, only the outer edge) and the inside's on another, with the same gate so they line up (where both would play, the outline's note is kept). It needs Channels: Multi channel; with the others it's all one channel and the box turns orange.
[clip:fill-outline]

Coloured areas: with Fill or Spam, the areas you coloured in the drawer (see Drawer: Areas) each get a colour of their own, and Empty ones get no notes. With Outline on, "Outline between colours" (under Fill and Spam) puts the notes where two colours meet on the outline too; unticked, the outline is only where the filled part ends. A shape has at most 15 colours (the outline and the plain fill count too): past that the extra colours share the 15th, and the panel says so in orange.

Outline gate (with Empty, Outline spam, or Fill / Spam set to Outline): makes the outline at least this many ticks thick, so it doesn't get thin where the shape is steep. It grows into the inside, so the shape's edge stays where it is; where the shape is thinner than that, all of it becomes outline. Even band shrinks the inside the same way on every side, top and bottom too, as the shape looked when it was first drawn: a circle or an arc shrinks into a smaller one even if you zoom differently now (then it can look uneven on screen, but it is right for the shape). Grow sideways just makes each short outline note longer toward the middle of its key. While you change the number, a red line on the piano roll shows where the inside now ends.

Overlaps cancel out (ticked unless you change it): where outlines overlap, the overlap stays empty, and a shape inside a shape makes a hole. Untick it to fill everything the lines close in: overlaps and holes too, also where one line crosses itself. (Text always fills its letters the way the font means them.)
Lines, curves and arcs can't be filled: turn them into a live shape first (Ctrl+R, see Turn into live shape).
Spiderweb asks before making more than a million notes.

help.custom_edit.title: Custom shapes: resize, turn, skew
help.custom_edit.tip: Drag a corner or side to resize, just outside a corner to turn, just outside a side's middle to skew. Drag inside to move it.
help.custom_edit.text: A selected custom shape (and text) shows a box. The mouse pointer changes to show what a drag will do.
Move: drag anywhere inside it (Select tool). It moves in grid steps; Shift = free.
Resize: drag a corner square. The opposite corner stays put; Ctrl keeps its proportions.
One side: drag a side (or its middle square) to move just that side.
Turn: drag from just outside a corner. It turns around its middle in 15° steps; Shift = any angle.
Skew: drag from just outside a side's middle. That side slides along itself in grid steps (Shift = free) while the opposite side stays.
Turning happens as the piano roll looks; zooming only one way afterwards slants it.
help.tumours.title: Tumours
help.tumours.tip: Bumps along the line: size, length, distance apart, rotation, which side. Length 0 = spikes (a zigzag). The … next to a number = a graph, so it changes along the line. Bumps take the current zoom's shape: zoom first, then set them up.
help.tumours.text: Select a line, polyline, freehand stroke, curve or arc, click Tumours… in the panel (or right-click it: Tumours…) and tick Tumours in the window that opens: bumps along it. Changes show on the piano roll at once: Accept (or Enter) keeps them as one undo step, X or Esc puts the lines back as they were, Reset puts every setting back to its default. The window can stay open; it shows whatever you select (selecting other shapes keeps what you did to the last ones). The line's points stay draggable; the line as drawn shows faint and dashed.
Shape: triangle, square, circle or parabola.
Size: how far the bumps stick out, in keys.
Length: how long each bump is along the line, in ticks. 0 = spikes (a zigzag).
Distance: from the start of one bump to the start of the next, in ticks.

Rotation: tilts every bump while its two feet stay on the line. Plus leans it forward (the way the line runs), minus leans it back; 90 lays it flat along the line, 180 turns it over to the other side.
Slant (square bumps only): 0 = a square, 100 = the top narrows to a point, minus = the top is wider than the bottom.

Graphs: the … button next to Size, Length, Distance, Rotation or Slant opens a graph of that number along the whole line (from its start on the left to its end on the right). 100 % = the number in the box, so the box still scales the whole graph. Drag the points (Shift = free), click to add one, or pick a preset or type a formula. Right-click a point: Value… types its exact place along the line and its value (in %, or as the number it makes), Delete point removes it (not when only two are left; deleting an end makes the next point the new end). Show picks how high the graph is shown, or type your own From / to. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo and redo the graph's changes while the window is open. The part outside the tumour Range is greyed out. A number following a graph says "× graph" in blue; Flat (off) removes it. The piano roll shows the change as you go; OK keeps it, Cancel (or Esc) puts the graph back as it was.
Side: alternating, left, right or random.

Straight or Bent with the line: this only matters where the line curves under a bump (long bumps on a curve, arc or circle). Straight builds each bump on a straight shortcut from where it starts to where it ends, so it looks angular. Bent with the line makes it follow the curve underneath, so the whole thing stays round. On a straight line both look the same.
Lead in: the bumps grow from nothing over that many ticks from each end, so the line eases into them.
Range: only part of the line gets bumps. Fit: a whole number of bumps fits exactly (seamless on a full circle).

The zoom matters: bumps are shaped as they look on screen when you change a tumour setting (a circle comes out round at that zoom). Zooming afterwards stretches them like the rest of the piano roll; changing any tumour setting again reshapes them for the zoom you're at now. So zoom to how you want to see them first, then set them up.

help.claw.title: Claw machine
help.claw.tip: Changes the selected shapes' notes: cuts slices of time out, or keeps some notes and trashes some. The shape stays as drawn, so you can move it, or open the claw again to change it or use it once more on top. Accept keeps it, X puts the notes back.
help.claw.text: The mouse wheel over a dropdown (Mode, Period, Trash every) picks the next or previous choice.

Select one or more shapes, then right-click one: Claw machine… (or press Alt+W). The notes change on the piano roll while you try settings. Accept keeps the change (one Ctrl+Z takes it back); X or Esc puts the notes back as they were. Reset sets the page back to the start, where it changes nothing.

Pages: each time you open the window it starts on +, a new page: change a setting and the page goes on top of the shape's other pages, working on the notes they left, so the same tool can be used again and again. The row at the top has a tab for each page this shape has (numbered by its place among all its Claw machine, Strum and Chop pages; the tab's tooltip shows the whole order). Click a tab to change that page, untick On to switch it off for now, or click the small × beside its tab to take it off (right-clicking a tab does both too).

You can keep working in the main window while it's open. It follows the selection: select other shapes to work on them. When you select other shapes or change something in the main window, the claw tried so far is kept (as its own Ctrl+Z step).

The pages are kept with the shape: the outline stays as you drew it, and moving, resizing or reshaping it makes new notes that go through the same pages again. Flipping or turning the shape (Turn 90°, or dragging just outside a custom shape's corner) flips or turns what they made, where it is; turned, each note becomes short notes on the key rows it crosses (a column of them for 90°), so there are more notes. Velocities drawn or typed afterwards replace theirs; a page added after that works on the new velocities.
Mode By time works like the claw machine found in other piano rolls:
Period: the claw works on this much time at a time, over and over, starting at the shape's first note.

Trash every: each period is cut into equal slices and one is thrown away. 1/4 = the first quarter, 2/4 = the second quarter, and so on. Notes in that slice go, notes crossing its edges are cut there, and all later notes move earlier to close the gap, so the notes end sooner.

Time dist: bends time inside each period. Turned right: long notes first, then faster and faster (a bouncing ball, a drum roll before a drop). Turned left: the other way round. Drag it up / down (Shift = fine), use the mouse wheel or the arrow keys; it stops at 0 for a moment on the way past. Hold the right mouse button on it to point it at the mouse. Middle-click (press the mouse wheel) puts it back to 0. It works even with Trash every at (none).
Stretch to compensate: stretches everything back to the shape's full length, so the notes get longer instead of ending sooner.
Remove short notes: removes the tiny pieces the claw leaves (under 1/24 beat). Notes that were that short already stay.

Count notes / Count keys / Count chords: keep some, then trash some, over and over to the end. Notes are counted in time order; keys are counted up from the shape's lowest key (keys with no notes count too), so every other key makes stripes; a chord = all the notes starting at the same moment.
Random: keeps about that many notes in every hundred. New random picks other notes; the same shape always gets the same pick.
Shorten instead of remove (not in By time): the notes picked to go stay, only shorter: this much of their length.
