help.strum.title: Strum
help.strum.tip: Makes the notes of each chord start one after another, like strumming a guitar: a straight edge of notes becomes a slope or a curve. The shape stays as drawn. Accept keeps it, X puts the notes back.
help.strum.text: Select one or more shapes, then right-click one: Strum… (or press Alt+S). The notes of each chord start one after another, like strumming a guitar, so a straight edge of notes becomes a slope or a curve. The notes change on the piano roll while you try settings. Accept keeps the change (one Ctrl+Z takes it back); X or Esc puts the notes back as they were. Reset sets the page back to the start, where it changes nothing.

Like the Claw machine, you can keep working in the main window while it's open, and the strum is a page kept with the shape: moving or reshaping it strums the new notes the same way. Each time the window opens it starts a new page (+); click a tab on top to change one the shape has, or the small × beside a tab to take it off. Pages work one after another, in the order they were added.
A chord = all the notes of a shape that start on the same tick (on a filled shape, each column of notes). A note on its own is left alone.

It works like the strum tool found in other piano rolls. Each knob has a box under it with its real value (times in ticks); type a number there to go past where the knob reaches. Turn a knob by dragging it up / down (Shift = fine), with the mouse wheel or the arrow keys; hold the right mouse button on it to point it at the mouse; middle-click puts it back to 0.

Start, Time: how much later each note starts than the one before. Turned right, the lowest note starts first; left, the highest. Tension: right = small steps first, each step bigger (100 = each twice the last); left = big steps first, each smaller (-100 = each half the last).

Start, Velocity: how much quieter each note is than the one before it in the strum. Turned left, it's the other way round: the last note keeps its velocity and the ones before it are quieter. Never under 1. Its Tension works like Time's.
Preserve end: the notes' ends stay where they were, so the notes get shorter instead of moving.
Trigger ahead: the strum happens before the chord instead of after it, so the last note lands where the chord started. Its tension works the other way round.
End, Time: the ends come earlier, one step more for each note. Turned right, the last note of the strum keeps its end; left, the first one does. A note that would end before it starts keeps 1 tick.
Start and End each have a box at the top to switch that whole part on or off.
Chop chords: wherever a note starts while other notes are still held, those notes are cut there, and the pieces strum again with it.
Alternate direction: every other chord strums the other way (notes on their own don't count).

help.chop.title: Chop (beta)
help.chop.tip: Cuts every note into a rhythm: even pieces, swing, off-beat, or one you draw. The shape stays as drawn. Accept keeps it, X puts the notes back.
help.chop.text: Beta: Chop is new and may still change in later versions.

Select one or more shapes, then right-click one: Chop… (or press Alt+U). Every note is cut into pieces in a rhythm, shown on the piano roll at once. Accept keeps it (one Ctrl+Z takes it back); X or Esc puts the notes back.
Quick chop (Ctrl+U, also in the right-click menu): cuts the notes into even pieces as long as the snap. With the snap off, the pieces are 1 tick long.
Rhythm: pick one from the list. The rhythm repeats along each note as many times as fits, and the last piece is whatever is left of the note. Empty parts of a rhythm leave gaps in the notes.

Draw your own in the strip under the list: press on empty space to put a piece there, as loud as the mouse is high, and drag to make it longer (sideways) or louder and quieter (up and down). Drag a piece up or down to change its velocity; its number shows while you drag. Right-click a piece to delete it, or right-drag to delete every piece the mouse passes over. Grid sets how finely you can draw (3 for triplets). Save… keeps it in the list under a name; Delete removes a saved one.
Steps: how long one repeat of the rhythm is. Step length: how long one step is, picked like the snap (shorter = a faster rhythm and more notes).

Velocity: "% of each note" (the start) makes every piece a share of its note's own velocity, so velocity ramps and changes you made stay; the dotted line is 100 % (the note's own), and dragging sticks to it (Shift = no sticking). "Fixed (1–127)" makes every piece exactly the velocity drawn, whatever its note had. Switching keeps the pieces about as loud (100 % = 127). Amount: how much the rhythm's velocities count. 0 = every piece keeps its note's velocity, 100 = fully. Quick chop never changes velocities.

Follow the song's grid (Absolute): on, the rhythm lines up with the song's beats, so a note that starts between them gets a short first piece. Off, the rhythm starts again at each note's start. In a shape with Fill, the notes that touch on one key (its outline notes, colour borders) count as one long note here, so the whole row follows one rhythm; spam notes each start their own.

Like the Claw machine, you can keep working in the main window while it's open, and the chop is a page kept with the shape: moving or reshaping it chops the new notes the same way. Opened on a shape that has no Chop page yet, the window chops at once; otherwise it starts on +, a new page (it's added once a setting changes). Click a tab on top to change a page the shape has, or the small × beside a tab to take it off. Quick chop adds a page too.
Order on one shape: Glue first, then the Claw machine, Strum and Chop pages in the order they were added.

help.slice.title: Slice (beta) (K)
help.slice.tip: Drag a straight line across shapes to cut them there. With a Select box drawn first, only what's inside the box is cut.
help.slice.text: Beta: Slice is new and may still change in later versions.

Pick Slice (K) and drag a straight line across shapes. When you let go, every line, polyline, freehand stroke, curve and arc it crosses is cut in two there (more pieces if it crosses more than once). The pieces stay where they were and end up selected.

Custom shapes (filled ones too) are cut in two when the line goes all the way across them: each half keeps its side of the drawing and gets the cut as a new edge, so a filled shape becomes two filled shapes. Areas coloured by hand stay with the half they're in. A spam gate Range is shared out: each half gets the part of it that was there, so the gates stay where they were. A line that only goes part of the way in leaves the shape whole.
Only some shapes or part of them: draw a Select box (or several, with Ctrl) first, then pick Slice. Only the shapes the boxes selected are cut, and only where the slice line is inside a box.
The line's ends go to the snap grid in time and between two keys, so a flat cut runs between key rows. Hold Shift to place them exactly. Text, pasted notes, Hz bass and funnels aren't cut.

A shape with glue or Claw machine, Strum or Chop pages is cut through its notes instead, wherever they are (they can sit far from the drawing): the line has to go all the way across them. Both pieces keep the whole drawing, one on top of the other until you move one. The pages are done before the cut, so the pieces look exactly as the shape did. Pages added to a piece afterwards work on that piece only. Once a piece's outline is changed (or Turn into a complete shape), it's a shape of its own: the shape's pages then work on its own notes, so its look may change (a piece of a shape with pages gets all its notes back).
One Ctrl+Z puts everything back as it was.

help.glue.title: Glue
help.glue.tip: Notes touching on the same key become one long note: fewer notes, the shape looks the same. Draw a Select box first to glue only the notes inside it.
help.glue.text: Select one or more shapes, then right-click one: Glue touching notes. On each key, notes that touch or overlap become one long note, from the first one's start to the last one's end. The shape looks the same with far fewer notes, for example a filled part with short gates.
Only some notes: draw a Select box (or several, with Ctrl) over the part to glue, then right-click inside the box: Glue touching notes in the box. A note is glued when its middle is in the box.
Notes with a gap between them, even one tick, stay apart. The glued note keeps the velocity of its first note. Notes of different colours don't glue together.

The glue is kept with the shape: moving, resizing or reshaping it glues the new notes the same way, and the boxes move and stretch with it. Glue another part to add to it. Right-click → Remove glue takes all of it off the selected shapes.
The glue comes first: Claw machine, Strum and Chop pages on the same shape work on the glued notes.

help.straighten.title: Straighten (freehand)
help.straighten.tip: 0 = as drawn. Higher = straighter lines, smoother curves, perfect shapes.
help.straighten.text: Freehand strokes (and freehand strokes in a live shape: pick the stroke first) have a Straighten number in the panel, 0-100.

0 = exactly as drawn. Higher = the stroke may stray further from your drawing to become simpler: wobbly parts become straight lines and smooth curves, sharp turns stay corners. A stroke that ends where it started becomes a perfect shape: circle or ellipse, square or rectangle, triangle (or another straight-sided shape). Turning it up makes it simpler (an oval → a circle, a rectangle → a square); a loop keeps its kind and its tilt.
The drawing is kept underneath, so you can change the number any time. New freehand strokes use the last number you picked.
help.straighten.words: smooth perfect recognise shape freehand sensitivity
help.curves_pen.title: Curves: anchors and handles
help.curves_pen.tip: Drag a round anchor to move it, drag a handle dot to bend. Alt = sharp corner. Right-click an anchor to remove it.
help.curves_pen.text: Curves (the Curve tool, funnel curves, curve strokes in the drawer and in live shapes) work like a pen tool.

Handles: drag the dot at the end of a blue handle line to steer the curve (its direction) and set how strongly it pulls (its length). On a smooth anchor both handles turn together. Handles can be dragged with any tool.
Anchors: drag an anchor to move it; its handles come along. The curve's two ends are anchors too (the squares, Select tool).
Adding and removing: middle-click the curve to add an anchor there (then drag it like any other). Right-click an anchor to remove it, or a handle dot to pull it back in (a corner).
Corners: Alt+drag a handle = move only that one (a sharp corner). Alt+drag an anchor = pull new handles out of it.
help.curves_pen.words: bezier pen anchor handle bend corner
help.symmetric.title: Symmetric halves
help.symmetric.tip: Right-click a curve: one half follows the other, mirrored (an arch) or turned (an S).
help.symmetric.text: Right-click a curve → Symmetric halves: one half follows the other. The curve gets an odd number of anchors with the middle one on the line of symmetry; editing one half rewrites the other.
Mirrored (like an arch): the second half is the first one reflected.
Turned half way round (like an S): the second half is the first one turned around the middle.
Off: the halves go their own way again.
help.join.title: Join and split
help.join.tip: Select several lines, polylines, freehand strokes, curves or arcs, then press Ctrl+G (or right-click). Right-click any of them → Split here cuts it in two.
help.join.text: Join: select two or more lines, polylines, freehand strokes, curves or arcs, then press Ctrl+G (or right-click one of them → Join shapes into one curve). They become one Curve shape: ends that touch are joined (with a corner there), and the curve's anchors and handles can be edited like any curve. Freehand strokes are turned into a smooth curve that follows them closely.

Shapes that don't touch stay separate pieces of the same curve: nothing is drawn between them and they make no notes there, but they're selected, moved, flipped and copied together. Each piece works like a shape of its own (its own row of tumours, range, graphs and last note). The squares at a piece's ends can't be removed.

Tumours: each shape keeps its own tumours after joining (even when they're the same), so no bump moves. The first time you change any tumour setting of the joined curve, the whole curve gets the settings shown in the tumour window, and the bumps run on across the joints. So set up each shape's tumours first, then join. Each shape keeps its velocities (where shapes play at the same time, the first selected one's win); Last note comes from the first shape.

Split here: right-click a line, polyline, freehand stroke, curve or arc where you want to cut it → Split here. On an anchor or a polyline point it's cut there; anywhere else a point is added there first. An arc becomes two arcs of the same circle; a freehand stroke is cut at its nearest drawn point (a straightened one is cut from the straightened line, and the halves are no longer straightened, so they look the same). Each half keeps the velocities it had, and its tumours stay where they were: each half gets its part of the Range and graphs (Fit is turned off, keeping the distance it had worked out). Only a bump across the cut is cut off, random sides are picked again and Lead in starts again at the cut.

Split into separate shapes (Ctrl+Shift+G, or right-click): a joined curve goes back to one curve per piece (and per shape that kept its own tumours). A custom shape, like one drawn with Live shape, splits into one shape per group of strokes that touch each other. Each part keeps the velocities it had.
Notes: a joined curve plays like one curve, so where two lines meet it doesn't start a new note the way two separate lines would.

help.funnel_curves.title: Funnel curves
help.funnel_curves.tip: Middle-click the line: a new curve start. Middle-click near a curve: an anchor. Select tool: click a curve again to highlight it (Del, right-click = shapes, linking).
help.funnel_curves.text: Middle-click on a funnel's line (any tool) to start curves there (a diamond); middle-click near a curve to add an anchor. The curves work like any curve: drag the anchors and handle dots (see Curves: anchors and handles). A start's two curves are linked, so they change together (see Linking funnel curves).

Highlighting: with the funnel selected and the Select tool, click one of its lines or curves again to highlight it (purple). A curve comes with the curves linked to it (teal); Ctrl+click adds or removes just one.
Del = delete it. Right-click = Formula (shapes and patterns, see Formulas), Back to the default curve, and linking.
Ctrl+H / Ctrl+J = flip the curves (end to end / inside out). Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V = copy a curve's shape onto others. Esc = clear the highlight.
help.funnel_curves.words: curve start anchor link mirror formula highlight
help.funnel_links.title: Linking funnel curves
help.funnel_links.tip: Linked curves change together (Ctrl while dragging = only this one). To link: Select tool, click a curve, Ctrl+click another, right-click → Link curves.
help.funnel_links.text: Linked curves change together: drag an anchor or handle on one and the others follow, and adding or removing an anchor does it on all of them. A new curve start's two curves come linked as mirror images of each other, so the funnel stays even on both sides.

Changing just one: hold Ctrl while dragging (or middle-clicking to add an anchor). If that gives it a different number of anchors than the others, it stops following them until they match again or you link them anew.
Linking curves yourself (any curves of one funnel, also on different lines):
1. Select the funnel, then with the Select tool click one of its curves: it's highlighted (purple), with the curves already linked to it (teal).
2. Ctrl+click more curves to add them (Ctrl+click a highlighted one to leave it out).
3. Right-click the curve whose shape you want to keep → Link curves:
Auto: each curve takes whichever way is closer to how it looks now.
Mirrored / Same shape (the name depends on which way the curves open): the same curve, reflected across the line or the same way round.
Flipped: turned end to end, so what happens near the start on one happens near the wall on the other.
Unlink: the highlighted curves go their own way.
The right-clicked curve keeps its shape, the others are reshaped to follow it. A curve can only be in one link group: linking it again takes it out of its old group.
Ctrl while drawing or dragging the wall keeps it centred on the line, so mirrored curves stay exact mirrors on the piano roll.
help.funnel_links.words: link linked unlink mirror mirrored flipped same shape together follow group ctrl
help.formulas.title: Formulas: shapes and patterns
help.formulas.tip: Right-click a curve, line, polyline or arc → Formula: give it a shape (Circle, Spiral, Heart…) or a pattern along it (Wave, Zigzag, Square wave, Spikes…). Live shape strokes, drawer strokes, funnel curves and polygon sides have it too.
help.formulas.text: Right-click a curve → Formula (a Curve tool curve, a line, a polyline, an arc, a stroke of a live shape or of the drawer, or highlighted funnel curves). It has two parts, and a curve can have both at once. (On a line, polyline or arc it works the same way: below, "curve" means them too. On a polyline the pattern runs along all of it, round its corners.)

Shape of the line: the line takes a shape. One that ends where it starts (Circle, Flower, Heart, Figure 8) is as wide as from the curve's start (A) to its end (B) and sits on that line; the others start at A and end at B. They're round as the piano roll looks when you pick them.

Pattern along the line: a pattern repeats along the line (along its shape, if it has one): Wave, Zigzag, Bounce, Square wave, Sawtooth, Teeth, Spikes, Half circles, Stair steps, Swell, Fading wave, Curls. Loops = how many times (4.5 works too). Its height is in keys. Curls: the line runs back over itself in little loops; "curl" over 1 makes loops, under 1 a wave.

Symmetric halves (in the Formula menu under each list, in the Custom… window and in the side panel): only the first half of the formula counts, and the second half is made from it: Mirrored (like an arch) or Turned half way round (like an S). A shape that ends where it starts stays closed. It works on your own formulas and saved ones too, and Save keeps it.

The curve you drew stays as a dashed line with its anchors and handles: bend it and the shape and pattern follow. The side panel shows the selected curve's numbers (like turns, petals, height and Loops). On a joined curve, Across all runs the loops on from piece to piece and Each piece gives every piece all of them. Separate curves each get their own pattern: join them first to run one pattern across them.

Custom… (at the top of each list) shows every shape or pattern with its formula and a box for each of its numbers. The preview shows one loop of a pattern, or the whole shape: drag its points to change it by hand, and every loop on the curve follows (Back to formula forgets it). Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo and redo your changes inside the window (Cancel still puts everything back). When its two halves match (like Wave, Bounce, S-curve or Circle), the points come as symmetric halves: moving a point moves its partner in the other half too. Double-click the line to add a point, right-click a point to remove it, Alt+drag for a sharp corner. The grid shows the numbers (x from 0 to 1 along one loop; y in keys); the mouse wheel zooms, dragging empty space (or middle-dragging) moves around, and Fit view shows all of it again. Save puts it in your list (patterns.json next to Spiderweb), and from then on it's in the Formula menu too.

Your own formula: tick Edit formula. A pattern is y of x for one loop (x goes from 0 to 1, y = how far to the side); a shape is x(t) and y(t), t going from 0 to 1 while it's drawn. Any other name in it (like height) gets its own number box. Works: numbers, + - * / ^ ( ), pi, e, sin cos tan asin acos atan sqrt exp ln log abs min max floor.

Remove formula takes them off (the curve you drew is left). Turn into plain curve makes what you see into ordinary anchors and handles (a line, polyline or arc becomes a curve); if its two halves match, it gets Symmetric halves.

A stroke of a live shape (or of any placed drawing): right-click the stroke on the piano roll. Its sizes are in keys as the piano roll looks when you pick it, and grow and shrink with the shape after that. The fill follows what you see, and new strokes snap onto the ends you see.

In the drawer, a pattern's sizes are hundredths of the board, so they grow and shrink with the placed shape. Funnel curves: a shape runs from the curve's start to its wall end inside the funnel (Slow start is x²); linked curves get the same formula; Back to the default curve resets it. Curve formulas saved in older versions (curves.json) are in the Shape list now.
The velocity pane has a Formula tool too: a line with a pattern swinging around it (see Velocity pane).

help.undo.title: Undo and redo
help.undo.tip: Made a mistake? Ctrl+Z = undo, Ctrl+Y = redo. Tick History in the toolbar to see every change as a step and jump back to any of them.
help.undo.text: Ctrl+Z undoes the last change, Ctrl+Y does it again. Ctrl+Z while something is half drawn drops just that.
Every change is a step with a name (the last 300 are kept). Tick History in the toolbar to see them all and click any step to jump straight to it (see History).
The drawer has its own Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y for its drawing.
help.undo.words: undo redo ctrl+z ctrl+y mistake back
help.history.title: History (undo steps)
help.history.tip: Every change is a step in the History list (tick History in the toolbar: it shows between Project and Shapes). Click a step to go back to it; Undock puts the list in a window of its own.
help.history.text: The History list (tick History in the toolbar; it shows in the side panel, between Project and Shapes) shows every change as a step, the oldest at the top: Start is how things were before the oldest step still kept (the last 300 are kept). The highlighted step is where you are now.

Click a step to go back to it: everything after it is undone and turns grey. Click a grey step to go forward again. Making a new change while steps are grey drops them (like Ctrl+Z and then changing something). Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y move up and down the same list. Typing in one box, or dragging a number box, is one step.
Undock puts the list in a window of its own that you can make taller; Dock (or closing that window) puts it back. Spiderweb remembers which, and where the window was.

help.selecting.title: Selecting, copying, flipping, turning
help.selecting.tip: Drag a box on empty space with Select, Ctrl+click = more shapes, Ctrl+A = all. Ctrl+C / V = copy / paste at the play line. Ctrl+H / J = flip, Ctrl+Left / Right = turn 90°.
help.selecting.text: With Select, drag on empty space: the box selects every shape it touches (Ctrl+drag adds them). The box snaps to the grid, out to the next grid line as soon as the mouse crosses one (Shift = no snap). Ctrl+click selects more shapes (also in the Shapes list), Ctrl+A selects all.

The box stays after you let go. Drag its sides or corners to stretch the shapes it selected (the other side stays put), or drag inside it to move them. Dragged past the edge of the piano roll, the view scrolls.

Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V: copy / paste at the play line (snapped to the grid); with Select, double-click empty space to paste there. Ctrl+C also puts the shapes on the clipboard as text, to share them (see Sharing shapes). Ctrl+D: duplicate. Del: delete.
Ctrl+H / Ctrl+J: flip sideways / upside down (sideways also mirrors velocities).
Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right: turn 90° as it looks on screen (the zoom decides how many beats a key becomes).
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y: undo / redo. While something is half drawn, Ctrl+Z just drops that.
Settings in the panel (velocity, last note…) change every selected shape.
help.selecting.words: box rectangle marquee area stretch scale resize copy paste duplicate flip mirror rotate turn undo redo delete
help.sharing.title: Sharing shapes
help.sharing.tip: Ctrl+C also copies shapes as one line of text: paste it anywhere to share them. Ctrl+V pastes a shared line. In the drawer: Export / Import.
help.sharing.text: Shapes can be shared as one line of text that starts with SPIDERWEB1:. Paste it anywhere as text to share it; whoever copies it can paste it into their own Spiderweb.

On the piano roll, Ctrl+C copies the selected shapes as before and also puts that line on the clipboard. Only the shapes go along, not the PPQ, BPM or other settings, so they look the same in any project.

Ctrl+V (or a Select double-click on empty space) pastes a shared line you copied after your last copy in Spiderweb: at the play line (or where you double-click), with the same spacing between the shapes. Otherwise it pastes what you copied in Spiderweb, as before.
The status bar says when the line is longer than 2,000 characters, since some places may not take that much at once. Shapes with many points or pasted notes make longer lines.

In the drawer, Export copies the whole drawing (its name, lines and coloured areas) as a line. Import adds a shared drawing to your shape library; if the name is taken, it gets a number, like "Star (2)". The drawing you're working on isn't touched.

Shared shapes can't be imported in the drawer, and shared drawings can't be pasted on the piano roll: Spiderweb says which one it is. A line that was cut off or changed is refused, so nothing half-broken gets in.
Text: if a text's font isn't installed on your PC, its letters stay as they were. The first time you change the text, Spiderweb asks, then redraws all of it in the default font (Arial on Windows).

help.numbers.title: Number boxes
help.numbers.tip: Drag a box's name sideways to change it, or press Up / Down in the box. Shift = big steps, Ctrl = small steps.
help.numbers.text: Every number box can be changed without typing: drag the name next to it sideways, or press Up / Down in it (the mouse wheel too, while you're typing in it). Shift = big steps, Ctrl = small steps. A name over two boxes (Velocity, Gate) changes both. Boxes also take math: 960*4, 1920/3…

help.view.title: Scrolling and zooming
help.view.tip: Wheel = scroll, Shift+wheel = sideways, middle-drag = scroll. Ctrl+wheel = zoom (Ctrl+Shift = time only, Alt = keys only). Fit view (top) = see everything.
help.view.text: Wheel = scroll up / down, Shift+wheel = sideways. Ctrl+wheel = zoom both ways, Ctrl+Shift+wheel = zoom time, Alt+wheel = zoom pitch. Middle-drag scrolls. Fit view shows everything. The zoom and scroll are remembered.

Scrollbars (under and right of the piano roll): drag the bar to scroll, drag one of its two ends to zoom, click beside it to go one screen that way. The − and + buttons at the end of each scrollbar zoom out / in. The bar under the piano roll reaches 8 bars past the last note.
Show lines / Show notes (top) hide the drawn lines or the notes. Keys outside a real 88-key piano are greyed on the keyboard.

Snap (top): the grid that points, moves and pastes snap to (Shift = free). Off, Bar, or a note length: a dot after the note = dotted (3/8 = a dotted quarter), a 3 = triplets (1/6 = quarter-note triplets). Custom… opens Customised snap: a number of notes (3 / 16 = three 16th notes), a dotted (.) or double-dotted (..) note, divided by a number (3 = triplets); it shows how long that is in beats and ticks.
help.view.words: zoom scroll pan fit view snap grid quantize quantise triplet dotted custom
help.velocity.title: Velocity pane
help.velocity.tip: Draw velocities over the bars: Linear, Curve, Pencil or Formula. With a shape selected only its notes change.
help.velocity.text: The pane under the piano roll shows every note's velocity. Draw over the bars with Linear, Curve, Pencil or Formula. With a shape selected, only its notes change (the others fade); with nothing selected, every note under the drag.

Formula: drag it like Linear; a pattern (Wave, Zigzag, Bounce or one you saved) swings the velocity up and down around the line. Pick the pattern, its Loops and height (in velocity steps) next to the tool buttons: changing them changes the line you just drew, until Enter or a click elsewhere.

Linear / Curve: drag it, then drag its end squares to move the ends (Ctrl = level with the other end) or a curve's round handle to bend it. Ctrl while drawing = flat. Hold Shift to snap the ends to the grid and, with a shape selected, onto its first / last note. Enter or a click outside the pane = done.
The velocities move and stretch with the shape. Typing a start / end velocity in the panel goes back to a straight ramp. Drag the bar above the pane to resize it; Velocity pane (top) hides it.
help.hz_live.title: Live keys (Hz bass)
help.hz_live.tip: This sound is NOT your MIDI. The live keys play a quick copy that Spiderweb makes from your soundfont's own notes, so you can try a Hz bass before placing it. Only notes you place in the Hz bass window go into your MIDI. It can sound a little different from a real render, most with soundfonts that change their sound at random.
help.hz_live.text: In the Hz bass window, press Synth… (it turns Preview on). The synth window has three tabs (the big buttons at the top left): OSC (the knobs), FX (the effects) and Draw (the effects' lines for one note, big), and a keyboard along the bottom.

Click and hold a key to hear the Hz bass of that key, as a note placed there would sound: its keys, gates and effects. Let go, and the falls after the sustain points play. Drag sideways to play other keys.

You can play with your computer's keyboard too, like a small piano: the middle row of letters A S D F G H J K are the white keys from C up, W E T Y U above them the black keys, and O L P ; go on past the next C.

Z and X move them an octave down or up; the keys they don't reach are greyed on the keyboard, and the line at the bottom says which they play. Hold a letter and turn a knob with the mouse to hear the change. The letters don't play while you type in a box.

Presets (next to the tabs) are ready-made sounds: click the name to pick one, or step through them with ◀ ▶. Save… keeps the sound you have as a preset of your own (every knob and line, not the notes), and Delete removes one of yours. A * after the name means you've changed the sound since picking it. Picking a preset can be undone like any change.

The meter at the top right shows how many notes a second the sound makes while one A1 is held: a higher note makes more, a lower one fewer, and Voices on Same keys, Echo, Reverb look-alike and Arpeggio add notes.

What you hear is NOT your MIDI. It's a quick copy made by Spiderweb: each different note is played once by the preview's synth with your soundfont, and copies of it are laid where the notes start. That's fast enough to play even a 128-key Hz bass live.
It sounds very close to the real thing with most soundfonts; a soundfont that changes its sound at random can't be copied exactly. Only notes you place in the Hz bass window go into your MIDI.

The first press after a change (another soundfont, new effects) waits a moment while the notes are recorded. The recordings are kept while Spiderweb is open; Preview settings… → Memory for live keys says how much memory they may take. When it's full, the ones used least are thrown away and recorded again when needed.
help.hz_live.words: hz bass live keys keyboard play hold preview quick sound fake copy synth window soundfont memory presets preset meter tabs
help.hz_osc.title: OSC tab (synth window)
help.hz_osc.tip: The OSC tab's knobs set the sound the way most synths do: Volume envelope, Wave, Pitch, Vibrato / Tremolo, Tone and Character.
help.hz_osc.text: The OSC tab of the synth window sets the sound the way most synths do. Every knob makes the effects' lines (Volume, the waveforms, Octave below, Pitch, Vibrato, Tremolo, Sweep, Wah, Slant, Groups, Off pitch, Noisy), so you can see them on the Draw tab and in the Hz bass window too, and they're in your MIDI. Voice and Arpeggio are settings of their own, not lines.

The light on each box's header is lit while that box changes the sound. Click the light or the box's name to switch the box off (bypass): its name goes grey and it does nothing, but its knobs are kept, and you can still turn them; click again to switch it back on.

Volume: Attack = how long the sound takes to get loud after you press a key, Decay = how long it then takes to drop to the Sustain level, Sustain = how loud it stays while you hold the key, Release = how long it fades out after you let go. Times are in beats. The picture under the knobs shows the envelope: the blue part is while the key is held, and a dot runs along it while a key sounds.

Wave: the Waveform and how much of it is used (Shape), and Octave below (every other wave softer, so the tone an octave lower comes in); the picture shows two waves' notes, one bar each, as tall as it hits.
Mode (in the Wave box) changes the shape of each wave one more way. Only the picked mode's knobs are shown.
FM = a fast wobble pushes the wave (metal or bell sounds); Time makes it die away after each note starts.
Pulse width = only the first part of each wave sounds, and Rate can make it open and close.
Sync = the wave starts over faster inside each wave: a hard, screaming sound.
Growl = every other wave lands a bit late: a lower tone under it.
Bitcrush = the notes moved onto a coarse grid: rough and gritty.
Pitch: each note starts Amount keys up (or down) and glides to its own tone in Time.
Vibrato and Tremolo (the LFOs, as synths call them) wobble the tone and the loudness: Rate = how many times a beat, Depth = how much, and Delay lets the vibrato come in slowly after each note starts.

Tone: Sweep makes one part of the shape's keys loud (Start) and can move it to End in Time after each note starts; Wah = loud and quiet stripes over the keys. The picture shows which keys are loud over time (darker = louder, the highest keys at the top).
Character: Slant, Groups, Off pitch and Noisy make the keys hit at different spots of the wave, which changes the colour of the tone; the picture shows eight keys' notes over four waves.

help.hz_voice.title: Voice and Arpeggio (synth window)
help.hz_voice.tip: Voice = copies of the sound, a little out of tune with each other, plus Glide and Legato. Arpeggio plays every note as a fast run.
help.hz_voice.text: Voice (in the OSC tab of the synth window): Voices = how many copies of the sound play together, Detune = how far out of tune they are with each other (in cents, 100 = one key).
Voices on = whether the keys take turns playing them (Split keys, no extra notes) or every key plays all of them (Same keys, more notes).
Glide = each note slides in from the tone of the note before it, taking that long (Only notes that touch: only when it starts right where that note ends).

Legato = a note that starts right where another ends carries on from it as one long note: no new Attack, and no Release until the last one ends (the effects that play once per note go on too). It works on the Arpeggio's notes as well: at Gate 100 % the whole run gets one envelope, under 100 % each note starts over.
The picture shows which copies eight keys play and a glide. Voice is a setting of its own, not a line.
Arpeggio (the third row of the OSC tab): switched on (click the light or the name on its header), every note you placed is played as a fast run of short notes, as a synth's arpeggiator does.

Pattern = the order (Up, Down, Up and down, Random), Speed = notes a beat, Octaves = how many octaves the run climbs through, Gate = how long each note is (100 % = touching), Chord = which notes: Notes placed together runs through a chord you placed, the others add a chord's notes to every note.
Each note of the run is a note of its own, so the Volume envelope and Glide work on each. Slides you made are left out while it's on. Like Voice, it's a setting of its own, not a line.

help.hz_fx.title: FX and Draw tabs (synth window)
help.hz_fx.tip: FX = a rack of Chorus, Echo and Reverb look-alike. Draw = the effects' lines for one note, big.
help.hz_fx.text: The FX tab of the synth window is a rack, as many synths have. The list on the left has every effect: click one to put it on the sound (it's lit, and shows on the right as a strip with its knobs and a picture), click it again to take it off, and drag one that's on up or down to change their order. The round button at the end of a strip switches the effect off without losing its knobs.
Chorus: every other key goes a little out of tune and back (Depth, Rate), a wide moving sound with no extra notes.
Echo: the whole sound comes again Repeats times, Time beats apart, each Fade as loud as the one before (one more set of notes each).

Reverb look-alike: after each note its tone rings on for Length beats, starting at Level and fading, its waves landing more and more out of place (Scatter). Real reverb can't be in a MIDI file; this only sounds a bit like it.
These are settings of their own too, not lines.

The lines on the Draw tab are the Hz bass window's own: drag points, add them and right-click them just like in its effects pane, and both change. An effect you put on there goes with each note, as in a synth: it plays once per note, and a repeating shape starts over at each note.

The note is drawn held for the longest line that plays once per note; its falls start at the "Let go" mark. While a key sounds, a dot runs along each line: it stops at the sustain point while you hold the key and runs down the fall when you let go.
The Hz bass window's effects pane shows the dots too, on the first note in view, and while the preview plays, a dot where the play line crosses each line.

help.playback.title: Playing and listening
help.playback.tip: Space = play / stop. Right-drag = listen to the notes under the mouse.
help.playback.text: Space (or Play) plays from the play line through the MIDI out picked under Project; the blue line follows and the view turns the page. Click or drag the bar numbers (or click empty space with Select) to move the play line. Playing stops a moment after the last note.

Built-in BASSMIDI (in the MIDI out list) plays through Spiderweb's own synth, with a soundfont you pick (the Hz bass preview uses the same one). Voices = how many sounds can ring at once: if playback stutters, lower it.
Right-drag (any tool) = listen to the notes under the mouse, like scrubbing.

help.channels.title: Channels
help.channels.tip: As drawn = everything kept. Single = one channel, overlaps fixed. Multi = overlapping shapes on different channels (each its own track).
help.channels.text: As drawn: every note exactly as the shapes make it, one channel; notes on the same key may overlap.

Single channel: where two notes on the same key overlap, the earlier one is cut where the later starts and the later one is stretched to where the earlier would have ended; notes starting on the same tick become one (the loudest, as long as the longest).

Multi channel: shapes whose notes clash go on different channels, each on its own track (channel 10, drums, is skipped). Split: Same key = only notes on the same key at the same time clash; Any notes = any notes at the same time. Shapes that follow one after another share a channel. Pasted notes (by track), live shapes made with Turn into live shape (by the shape each stroke came from) and Fill / Spam set to Outline (the outline and the inside) can spread over several channels: the shape list says how many, in orange above 15 (from there the colours and channel numbers repeat).
Every channel has its own note colour.

Colours (in the side panel, under Velocity): any shape's notes take turns over several channels, so its colour keeps changing. By step = each step the next channel (spam: each gate column; lines: each note in time), By key = each key, By time = every note length from the start of the song (1/4 = a beat, so it lines up with the bar lines). Channels = how many take turns, every = how long one lasts. Each key row (By step / By time, Spam and Outline spam shapes only): From its start = each key row starts again at the first channel where its notes begin (after a gap too), so the colours follow the shape's left edge; From its end = counted back from each row's last note, so they follow the right edge. It needs Multi channel. Which colours you see depends on the program showing the MIDI.

help.files.title: Saving and MIDI export
help.files.tip: Your work saves itself. Generate MIDI writes the .mid file set under Project.
help.files.text: Everything is saved on its own (autosave.json next to Spiderweb) and comes back next time; each time Spiderweb starts, the previous session is kept as autosave-backup.json. Save… / Open… keep and open project files (.json). Opening one replaces what's on the piano roll (Undo can't bring it back), so if your shapes aren't saved in a project file, Spiderweb asks to save them first. Shapes are stored in beats, so changing PPQ doesn't move them.
Generate MIDI writes the file set under Output file, with the PPQ, BPM and beats per bar from Project. PPQ 32767 or higher: many MIDI programs can't open the file (the box turns red).

Keys (under Project) set to 256: the piano roll goes up to key 255 instead of 127, and the MIDI file keeps those keys. That's for players that support 256 keys (handy for tunings like 31edo, which need more keys per octave). Many MIDI programs can't read keys above 127, and playback here skips them. Back at 128, notes above 127 are left out; the shapes stay as they are.
If something goes wrong, the details go to errors.log next to Spiderweb.

help.domino.title: Copy to / Paste from Domino
help.domino.tip: Ctrl+Shift+C copies the notes; paste them in Domino with Ctrl+V. Ctrl+Shift+V pastes notes copied in Domino as one shape.
help.domino.text: Copy to Domino (under Project, or Ctrl+Shift+C) puts the selected shapes' notes on the clipboard, or all notes when nothing is selected. In Domino, pick the track and press Ctrl+V, or double-click where the notes should go.
The dropdown above the buttons sets where the notes start, for copying and pasting both:
• First note at tick 0: the first note lands right on Domino's cursor (or on the play line here).
• From the bar line: the empty space from the bar line before the first note comes along, so paste on a bar line and the notes keep their place in the bar.
As drawn / Single channel: everything goes into the track you paste into, on that track's channel.

Multi channel: each channel with notes becomes a track, in channel order, packed together (channels without notes are skipped): the first goes into the track you paste into, the next into the track below it, and so on. The pasted notes play on those tracks' own channels, and tracks that don't fit below the last one are dropped.

Ticks are copied as they are: with a different PPQ in Domino the notes come out longer or shorter, so set the same PPQ in both (or use that on purpose). With 256 keys, notes above key 127 are left out (Domino has 128 keys).

Paste from Domino (or Ctrl+Shift+V) works the other way: select notes in Domino, press Ctrl+C there, then paste here. The start of what you copied (or its first note, see the dropdown) lands on the play line (snapped to the grid), like pasting in Domino, and ticks are taken as they are. The notes of every copied track become ONE shape (Pasted notes); controllers and other events are left out. Each note remembers its track: with Multi channel every track gets a channel of its own (even tracks that never overlap), with Single channel all of them go on one channel and overlaps are removed. If Ctrl+Shift+V does nothing, another program (often a clipboard manager) has taken that shortcut for itself: free it in that program's settings, or use the button.

Move, flip, turn, stretch or skew the shape like a custom shape: the notes go with its box. The notes keep their own velocities until you change the shape's velocity (in the panel or the velocity pane).

help.drawer.title: The drawer
help.drawer.tip: Draw a shape for your library, Save it, then Use on the piano roll. Closed outlines can be filled.
help.drawer.text: The drawer (Custom shape → Drawer…) is where you draw shapes for your library. Its tools work like the piano roll's: Select (V), Eraser (E), Line (L), Polyline (P), Freehand (F), Curve (C), Arc (A), Square (S) and Circle (O). Areas (B) colours the areas inside (see Drawer: Areas). Points stick to other strokes when the mouse is near them: to their points first, then to where two lines cross, then anywhere along a line (a purple mark shows where). A point stuck to a line is exactly on it, so the outline counts as closed there. Away from lines, points snap to the grid. Shift draws freely. Drag a stroke out, or click where it starts and click where it ends (right-click or Esc cancels).

Mirror (next to Grid): every new stroke gets a mirrored copy across the middle of the board, shown while you draw. Horizontal mirrors left ↔ right, Vertical top ↔ bottom, Both into all four corners. The board's grey side is where the copies go, and a blue-green line marks the middle. Points stick to that line (on the grid along it), and halves whose ends meet on it join up into one outline (a half heart becomes a whole closed heart). The copies are normal strokes: change them on their own afterwards.

Layers (bottom right) lists every stroke, the last drawn on top. Click a row to pick that stroke (Ctrl / Shift+click picks several); picking on the board picks the rows too. Drag rows up or down to change the order. Double-click a name (or F2) to rename it; an empty name gives it back its own. Del deletes the picked strokes. The eye shows or hides a stroke: hidden strokes aren't drawn and are left out of the shape on the piano roll, but stay in the saved drawing (the drawer warns while any are hidden). Alt+click an eye to show only that stroke; Alt+click it again to show them all. The lock keeps a stroke from being picked, moved or erased on the board (other strokes still stick to it). Right-click a stroke (on the board or in the list) for Invert selection, Hide selected and Lock selected.

Groups: pick some strokes, right-click one (on the board or in Layers) > Group. The group gets a folder row (click its arrow to fold it away); its eye and lock work on all of its strokes, and double-clicking its name renames it. Clicking a grouped stroke on the board picks the whole group, so it moves, flips and turns as one; Ctrl+click picks a single stroke. Drag rows into a group or out of it in Layers, or drag the group's row to move it all. Right-click > Ungroup takes the group apart (the strokes stay). Pasted copies aren't in a group.
Save keeps it in the library (the shapes subfolder next to Spiderweb); Use on the piano roll picks it for the Custom shape tool. On the piano roll it stretches to the box you drag.

Rename (or F2, or click the picked name again) changes a saved shape's name; Delete removes it. While the list has the keyboard (its picked name is blue), Delete and Enter work on the list; click the board to give the keyboard back to the drawing (the picked name turns grey).
Export copies the whole drawing as a line of text to share; Import adds a shared drawing to your library (see Sharing shapes).

Lines and curves that meet end to end count as one outline, and so does a line whose ends land on another line or on itself. Closed: Empty, Fill and Spam all work. Gaps (red dots at the loose ends): Fill and Spam close each one with a straight line (see Inside fill).
Wheel = zoom, middle-drag = scroll, Reset view = back to the middle of the board.
help.drawer_select.title: Drawer: Select and editing
help.drawer_select.tip: Drag a point (small squares) or a stroke. Drag on empty space = a box selecting several. Del = delete.
help.drawer_select.text: Select: drag a point (small squares; points in the same spot move together, so outlines stay closed), an ellipse's corners, or a whole stroke (moves in grid squares, Shift = free). Dragged points stick to other strokes like new ones; one stroke moved on its own sticks by its point nearest to another stroke, and by its line too: another stroke's point comes onto it, or it rests against another stroke's line (a circle touches a slanted line instead of crossing it). Between two lines it can also rest on both at once (a smaller reach, with a mark at each touch). Drag on empty space to draw a box: every stroke it touches is selected, and the box stays until you click outside it. Ctrl+drag adds another box, Ctrl+click adds or removes one stroke. Dragging one of the selected strokes, or anywhere inside the box, moves them all; right-click inside the box (or on one of them) for what works on all of them at once. A click on empty space deselects. Del deletes the selected strokes. Middle-drag scrolls.
Right-click a stroke = its menu (add point / anchor, symmetric curve halves, its role, delete, copy, paste, flip, turn); empty space = deselect; while drawing a polyline = finish it.

A stroke's role: Outline and fill (normal) makes notes and makes the inside for Fill and Spam. Outline only (dotted) makes notes on top of the fill, but cuts no hole and closes no gap. Fill line (thin dashes) makes no notes and doesn't change what's filled: it splits the inside into areas you can give their own colour.

Outline colour: the stroke's notes go in that colour (a channel of their own with Multi channel; the same numbers as the Areas tool's, so colour 2 here and an area in colour 2 share a channel). It counts where the stroke's own notes are: Empty and Outline spam, and Outline only strokes with Fill and Spam (the edge of a filled area is the fill's).

Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V = copy / paste (each paste lands one more grid square down and right), Ctrl+H / Ctrl+J = flip sideways / upside down, Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right = turn 90°. These work on the selected strokes, or the whole drawing when nothing is selected. Pasted strokes come out selected, so they can be moved together.

help.drawer_line.title: Drawer: Line
help.drawer_line.tip: Drag from start to end, or click both.
help.drawer_line.text: Drag from start to end, or click the start and click the end. Right-click it: Formula (a shape or a pattern along it, see Formulas).
help.drawer_poly.title: Drawer: Polyline
help.drawer_poly.tip: Click points (or drag each piece). Click the first point again to close it.
help.drawer_poly.text: Click points, or drag each piece. Click the first point again to close it; double-click or right-click stops. Right-click it: Formula (a shape or a pattern along it, see Formulas).
help.drawer_free.title: Drawer: Freehand
help.drawer_free.tip: Drag to draw. Let go near the start to close it.
help.drawer_free.text: Hold the mouse button and draw. Letting go near the start closes it.
help.drawer_curve.title: Drawer: Curve
help.drawer_curve.tip: From start to end, then bend it with its blue handles. Middle-click it = new anchor.
help.drawer_curve.text: Drag (or click) from start to end. The new curve is selected: bend it with its handles like any curve (see Curves: anchors and handles); middle-click near it adds an anchor. Right-click it: Formula (a shape or a pattern along it, see Formulas).
help.drawer_arc.title: Drawer: Arc
help.drawer_arc.tip: Click start, a point it passes through, end. Or drag start to end, then click to bend.
help.drawer_arc.text: Click its start, a point it passes through, then its end (or drag from start to end, then click to set the bend): a piece of a perfect circle. End on the start = a whole circle. Select: drag its three points. Right-click it: Formula (a shape or a pattern along it, see Formulas).
help.drawer_square.title: Drawer: Square
help.drawer_square.tip: Corner to corner. Ctrl = a perfect square.
help.drawer_square.text: Drag (or click) corner to corner; Ctrl makes it a perfect square. While you drag, its sides stick too: near another stroke's slanted or curved line the square grows or shrinks until it rests on it (a corner on the line, or a side against a curve) (not with Ctrl; Shift = free). Between two lines it can rest on both at once (a smaller reach, with a mark at each touch). The corner under the mouse sticking to a point or a crossing still comes first.
help.drawer_circle.title: Drawer: Circle
help.drawer_circle.tip: Corner to corner. Ctrl = a perfect circle.
help.drawer_circle.text: Drag (or click) corner to corner of its box; Ctrl makes it a perfect circle. While you drag, the circle's own line sticks: near another stroke's line or point it grows or shrinks until it touches exactly (Shift = free). A little further away, a dotted purple point shows where to point the mouse for it to touch, on a faint dotted copy of the line it would touch. Between two lines (a roof, a corner) a second point shows where it rests on both at once: the circle becomes an oval to fit (not with Ctrl). With Mirror on, it rests on the mirror line too, so it touches its copy.
help.drawer_erase.title: Drawer: Eraser
help.drawer_erase.tip: Click a stroke to remove it, or drag a box: every stroke it touches goes. Ctrl+Z = undo.
help.drawer_erase.text: Click a stroke to remove it, or drag a box: when you let go, every stroke it touches is removed. Right-click or Esc while dragging drops the box without removing anything. Ctrl+Z brings back everything one box removed.
help.drawer_areas.title: Drawer: Areas
help.drawer_areas.tip: Click an area to give it the colour picked on the right (or Empty), or drag across several. Right-click = back to normal.
help.drawer_areas.text: Areas are the pieces your lines cut the drawing into. Grey = what Fill and Spam fill as normal. Pick a colour on the right (or Empty), then click an area to give it that colour, or hold the button and drag to colour every area you pass over. Right-click an area to put it back to normal; "Reset all colours" puts every area back. Each area keeps its colour when you move or change lines, and when the shape is placed and stretched.

On the piano roll the colours count only with Fill or Spam. Each colour number gets a channel of its own with Multi channel, so it shows in a colour of its own there too (the piano roll picks those colours, so they can differ from the drawer's). Areas with the same number share a channel. Empty leaves an area without notes; a coloured hole gets filled.

The line under the colours says how many colours the shape will use, with and without "Outline" on (the shape's own colour counts too, where an area is left as normal). A shape has at most 15: past that the line turns orange, and on the piano roll the extra colours share the last one.
To split an area without adding notes, draw a fill line through it (right-click the stroke → Fill line). Lines that end a bit past an edge split best.
Very thin slivers may take the colour of the area next to them.
help.drawer_areas.words: drawer area colour color channel fill paint bucket zone track
help.shortcuts.title: Keyboard and mouse shortcuts
help.shortcuts.tip: Every key and mouse shortcut in one list.
help.shortcuts.text: Tools: V Select, K Slice, L Line, P Polyline, F Freehand, C Curve, A Arc, S Custom shape, O Circle, Q Polygon, N Funnel, X Text, H Hz bass. G = Live shape on / off.
Drawing: Shift = don't snap. Ctrl = perfect (circle, equal-sided polygon or star, proportions). Right-click or Esc = cancel what's half drawn. Enter / double-click = finish a polyline.

Mouse: right-click a shape = its menu, empty space = deselect. Double right-click = Select ↔ last tool. Right-drag = listen. Middle-click = add a point / anchor / funnel curve start. Middle-drag = scroll.
Wheel = scroll, Shift+wheel = sideways, Ctrl+wheel = zoom, Ctrl+Shift+wheel = zoom time, Alt+wheel = zoom pitch.

Editing: Del delete, Ctrl+D duplicate, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo / redo (see History), Ctrl+A select all, Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V copy / paste, Ctrl+H / Ctrl+J flip, Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right turn 90°, Ctrl+G join into one curve, Ctrl+Shift+G split into separate shapes, Ctrl+R turn into live shape, Alt+W claw machine, Alt+S strum, Alt+U chop, Ctrl+U quick chop, Esc clear highlight / unpick a stroke. With a stroke of a live shape picked, the copy / paste / flip / turn keys work on that stroke.
Playing: Space play / stop. Click or drag the bar numbers = move the play line.
Curves: Alt+drag a handle = sharp corner, Alt+drag an anchor = new handles, Ctrl = change only this curve (linked funnel curves).
Number boxes: drag the name, Up / Down, wheel; Shift = big steps, Ctrl = small.
F1 = Help. Ctrl+S = save. Ctrl+Shift+C = Copy to Domino, Ctrl+Shift+V = Paste from Domino.
panel_custom.not_in_library: This shape isn't in the shape library any more (renamed or deleted). Its drawing is kept in this project.
claw.n_shapes: {n} shapes (they all get the same settings)
claw.tip_mode:
How the notes are picked:
By time: cuts slices of time out, like the claw machine of other piano rolls.
Count notes / keys / chords: keep some, trash some, over and over (notes starting together = one chord).
Random: keeps notes picked at random.
claw.tip_keep: How many to keep before trashing some.
claw.tip_skip: How many to throw away after the ones kept. 0 = keep everything.
claw.tip_pct: About this many notes in every hundred stay; which ones is random.
claw.tip_new_random: Pick other notes at random (the same number of them).
claw.tip_shorten: The notes picked to go stay, only shorter.
claw.tip_cut: How long they stay: this much of their length (at least 1 tick).
claw.tip_period: The claw works on this much time at a time, over and over, starting at the shape's first note.
claw.tip_trash:
Cuts each period into equal slices and throws one away: 1/4 = the first quarter, 2/4 = the second quarter, and so on.
Notes in it go, notes crossing its edges are cut, and the later notes move earlier to close the gap.
claw.tip_dist:
Bends time inside each period.
Right: long notes first, then faster and faster. Left: the other way round.
Drag up / down (Shift = fine), mouse wheel or arrow keys; it stops at 0 for a moment on the way past.
Right mouse button: points it at the mouse. Middle-click (press the wheel) = back to 0.
claw.tip_stretch: Stretches the result back to the shape's full length (the notes get longer too).
claw.tip_short: Removes notes the claw left very short (under 1/24 beat). Notes that were that short already stay.
claw.tip_reset: Everything back to the start (the claw then changes nothing).
range_window.title: Spam gate range
range_window.from_tip: The first gate: where the graph is at the bottom. It's the shape's spam gate (the gate box in the side panel).
range_window.to_tip: The second gate: where the graph reaches the top.
range_window.dir_tip: Left to right: every key is cut at the same places, the gate changing over time. Low to high / Top to bottom: each key has its own gate, from the lowest key to the highest, or from the highest to the lowest.
range_window.rows_tip: Every key row goes from the first gate to the second along its own length, short or long, instead of along the whole shape. Where a row crosses the shape more than once, each piece runs the whole range. A row too short for any note gets one note of the first gate. Left to right only.
range_window.join_tip: A row that crosses the shape more than once runs the range once, from its first piece to its last, gaps included, instead of starting over on each piece.
range_window.fit_tip: Each row's first and last note reach exactly to the shape's edges: stretched over the blank left at an end, or trimmed where a long gate would stick out.
range_window.hint: Bottom = the first gate, top = the second. Drag a point to move it (Shift = free), click the line or empty space to add one, right-click a point to delete it. The pale steps are the whole-tick gates the notes get. Straight = every gate gets an equal share, so most notes are the short ones.
chop.n_shapes: {n} shapes (they all get the same settings)
chop.tip_rhythm: The rhythm every note is cut into. It repeats along each note, as many times as fits.
chop.tip_save: Keep this rhythm under a name: it shows at the bottom of the Rhythm list from now on.
chop.no_pieces: No pieces in the rhythm: the notes aren't chopped.
chop.name_taken: "{name}" is a built-in rhythm's name. Pick another name:
chop.tip_strip: One repeat of the rhythm. Press on empty space to put a piece there, as loud as the mouse is high; drag to make it longer or change its velocity. Drag a piece up or down to make it louder or quieter (in %, the dotted line = the note's own velocity). Right-click (or right-drag) to delete pieces. Empty space = a gap in the notes.
chop.tip_grid: How many grid cells each step has in the strip above (3 for triplets). Only for drawing.
chop.tip_steps: How many steps one repeat of the rhythm lasts.
chop.tip_step_length: How long one step is, picked like the snap. Shorter = faster rhythm, more notes. Off = 1 tick.
chop.tip_velocity: Amount: how much the rhythm's own velocities count. 0 = every piece keeps its note's velocity, 100 = the rhythm's velocities fully.
chop.tip_mode: % of each note: every piece is a share of its note's own velocity, so velocity ramps stay. Fixed: every piece is exactly the velocity drawn. Switching keeps the pieces about as loud (100 % = 127).
chop.tip_absolute: On: the rhythm lines up with the song's beats, so a note starting between them gets a short first piece. Off: the rhythm starts again at each note's start.
chop.too_many: Too many pieces to make: the notes are left unchopped. Pick a longer step length.
chop.tip_reset: Back to the start: the Even rhythm, 1/16 steps.
chop.quick_done: Quick chop: notes cut into {snap} pieces. Right-click → Chop… (Alt+U) changes or removes it
strum.n_shapes: {n} shapes (they all get the same settings)
strum.tip_start: Switches the Start part on or off: when the notes start, and their velocity.
strum.tip_end: Switches the End part on or off: when the notes end.
strum.tip_time:
How much later each note starts than the one before (in ticks).
Right: the lowest note first. Left: the highest note first.
strum.tip_tension:
Right: small steps first, each one bigger. Left: big steps first, each one smaller.
100 = each step twice the last, -100 = half.
strum.tip_vel:
How much quieter each note is than the one before it (in velocity).
Left: the other way round, the last note keeps its velocity. Never under 1.
strum.tip_vel_tension: Right: small changes first, each one bigger. Left: big changes first, each one smaller.
strum.tip_end_time:
How much earlier each note ends than the next one (in ticks).
Right: the last note of the strum keeps its end. Left: the first one does.
strum.tip_end_tension: Right: small steps first, each one bigger. Left: big steps first, each one smaller.
strum.tip_preserve: The ends stay where they were: the notes get shorter instead of moving.
strum.tip_ahead: The strum happens before the chord: the last note lands where the chord started.
strum.tip_chop: Where a note starts while others are still held, those are cut there and strum again with it.
strum.tip_alternate: Every other chord strums the other way (notes on their own don't count).
strum.tip_reset: Everything back to the start (the strum then changes nothing).
strum.tip_knob: Drag up / down (Shift = fine), mouse wheel or arrow keys. Right mouse button: points it at the mouse. Middle-click = back to 0. Or type a value in the box under it.

tool_window.differ: The selected shapes have different pages: a change goes on a new page on each.
tool_window.tip_on: Untick to switch this page off for now: it's kept, but changes nothing.
tool_window.tip_remove: Remove: takes this page off the selected shapes. The pages after it then work on the notes left before it.

hz.synth_tip: A window like a synth's: knobs for the sound, the effects' lines for one note, and a keyboard to hear the Hz bass live (a quick copy made from your soundfont, not your MIDI).
hz.synth_warning: What you hear here is a quick copy made from your soundfont, NOT your MIDI. Place notes in the Hz bass window to keep them.
hz.synth_hint: Click and hold a key below to hear it. These are the Hz bass window's own effects, shown for one note.
hz.synth_hint_knobs: Turn a knob, then click and hold a key below to hear it.
hz.synth_letters: Letters A to ; play {lo} to {hi} (Z / X: an octave down / up).
hz.synth_tip_mode: Mode: one more way to change the shape of each wave. FM = the wave is pushed back and forth by a fast wobble (a metal or bell-like sound). Pulse width = only the first part of each wave sounds (a hollow, nasal sound). Sync = the wave starts over faster inside each wave (a hard, screaming sound). Growl = every other wave lands a bit late, so a lower tone growls under it. Bitcrush = the notes are moved onto a coarse grid (rough and gritty). FM, Pulse width and Sync make up to 16 notes a wave; Growl and Bitcrush add none.
hz.synth_tip_fm_depth: Depth: how hard the wobble pushes the wave. 0 = no change. Works on the Waveform picked (with Plain it uses a sine).
hz.synth_tip_fm_ratio: Ratio: how fast the wobble is, times the note's tone. Whole numbers (1, 2, 3...) sound in tune; others sound like a bell or metal.
hz.synth_tip_fm_time: Time: the wobble dies away over this long after each note starts, so the note starts bright and settles (an FM bass pluck). 0 = it stays.
hz.synth_tip_pulse_width: Width: how much of each wave sounds. 50 % = a square wave, less = thinner and more nasal.
hz.synth_tip_pulse_rate: Rate: how many times a beat the width opens up to 50 % and back (the classic moving pulse sound). 0 = it stays still.
hz.synth_tip_sync_amount: Amount: how many times faster the wave starts over inside each wave of the note's tone. The note's tone stays the same; the colour changes a lot.
hz.synth_tip_sync_time: Time: the amount rises from 1 to its full value over this long after each note starts (the sweeping sync sound). 0 = full at once.
hz.synth_tip_growl_amount: Amount: how late every other wave lands. 100 % = half a wave. No extra notes.
hz.synth_tip_growl_every: Every: the late waves take turns over this many waves: 2 = a tone an octave lower comes in, 3 = lower still.
hz.synth_tip_crush_amount: Amount: how coarse the grid the notes are moved onto is. The more, the rougher. No extra notes.
hz.synth_tab_knobs_tip: OSC: the sound's main settings (wave, volume, pitch, LFOs, tone, voices, arpeggio).
hz.synth_tab_effects_tip: The effects on the sound: Chorus, Echo, Reverb look-alike.
hz.synth_tab_lines_tip: The effects' lines for one note, big: drag their points, as in the Hz bass window.
hz.synth_meter_tip: How many notes a second this sound makes while one {key} is held (its first 4 beats). A higher note makes more, a lower one fewer; Voices on Same keys, Echo, Reverb look-alike and Arpeggio add notes.
hz.rack_empty: No effects yet. Click one in the list on the left to put it on: Chorus, Echo or Reverb look-alike.
hz.rack_list_tip: Every effect. Click one to put it on the sound (lit: its strip shows on the right) or to take it off again. Drag one that's on up or down to change their order.
hz.rack_on_tip: Switches the effect off (or on again) without losing its knobs, to hear the sound without it.
hz.rack_reverb_notes: a fading tail after each note
hz.synth_tip_chorus_depth: Depth: how far out of tune every other key goes, in cents (100 = one key). A little sounds wide and moving.
hz.synth_tip_chorus_rate: Rate: how many times a beat it goes out of tune and back. 0 = no chorus.
hz.synth_tip_echo_time: Time: how long after the sound each repeat comes, in beats (0.75 = a dotted eighth).
hz.synth_tip_echo_repeats: Repeats: how many times the sound comes again. Each repeat is one more set of notes.
hz.synth_tip_echo_fade: Fade: how loud each repeat is, next to the one before it. 100 % = as loud, 0 = no repeats.
hz.synth_tip_reverb_length: Length: how long each note's tone rings on after the note ends, in beats.
hz.synth_tip_reverb_scatter: Scatter: how much the ringing tone's waves land out of place as it fades, like a room's echoes blurring together. 0 = it stays clean.
hz.synth_tip_reverb_level: Level: how loud the ringing starts, next to the note. It fades from there.
hz.synth_tip_arp_on: Click to switch the arpeggio on or off. On (lit): every note (or chord) you placed is played as a fast run of short notes instead. Turning one of its knobs or picking a Pattern or Chord switches it on too.
hz.synth_tip_lamp: Lit while this box changes the sound. Click it (or the box's name) to switch the box off: its knobs are kept, but it does nothing (bypass). Click again to switch it back on.
hz.synth_tip_arp_pattern: Pattern: the order of the run. Up = low to high, Down = high to low, Up and down = back and forth, Random = any order.
hz.synth_tip_arp_chord: Chord: which notes the run goes through. Notes placed together = the notes of a chord you placed (a single note just goes through its Octaves). The others add that chord's notes to every note you placed.
hz.synth_tip_arp_speed: Speed: how many notes a beat the run plays (4 = sixteenth notes).
hz.synth_tip_arp_octaves: Octaves: the run goes through its notes in this many octaves, one after the other. 1 = just the notes.
hz.synth_tip_arp_gate: Gate: how long each note of the run is, next to the time until the next one. 100 % = they touch (Glide can slide between them); less = short, plucky notes.
hz.synth_tip_voices: Voices: how many copies of the sound play together, each a little out of tune with the others (Detune). They beat against each other: a thicker, wider sound. 1 = just the sound.
hz.synth_tip_detune: Detune: how far apart the highest and the lowest copy are, in cents (100 cents = one key). The others are spread evenly between them. A little (10-30) sounds thick, a lot sounds out of tune.
hz.synth_tip_voices_on: Voices on: Split keys = the shape's keys take turns playing the copies, one copy each (no extra notes). Same keys = every key plays every copy, so the copies drift in and out of each other (as many times the notes as there are voices).
hz.synth_tip_glide: Glide: each note slides in from the tone of the note before it, taking this long. 0 = no glide. Each note still starts its own envelope. No glide from a note of the same tone, or into a note a slide you made reaches.
hz.synth_tip_legato: A note that starts right where another ends carries on from it, as one long note: the envelopes don't start over (no new Attack), and the first note doesn't fade out (no Release) until the last one ends. With the Arpeggio at Gate 100 %, the whole run gets one envelope. Notes with a gap between them still start over.
hz.synth_tip_touching: Only notes that touch: a note glides only when it starts right where the note before it ends. Off = it glides even after a gap.
hz.synth_tip_sweep: Sweep: one part of the shape's keys is loud and the others get quieter, and that part can move while the note sounds. Turning one of its knobs ticks On too.
hz.synth_tip_sweep_start: Start: where the loud part is when a note starts. 0 % = the lowest keys, 100 % = the highest.
hz.synth_tip_sweep_end: End: where it moves to. The same as Start = it stays still.
hz.synth_tip_sweep_time: Time: how long it takes to move from Start to End after each note starts. 0 = it stays at Start.
hz.synth_tip_wah: Wah: loud and quiet stripes over the keys, more stripes the more it's turned. 0 = every key full. Strongest together with Slant.
hz.synth_tip_slant: Slant: every key starts a little later than the key below it. 100 % = spread over one whole wave. No extra notes.
hz.synth_tip_groups: Groups: the keys take turns in this many groups. 1 = all together. No extra notes.
hz.synth_tip_offpitch: Off pitch: every key repeats a little slower or faster than the tone, so the keys drift apart and meet again by themselves. 100 % = 2 % between the lowest and the highest key.
hz.preset_tip: Presets: ready-made sounds. Click to pick one: ours first, then the ones you saved. A * after the name means the sound has been changed since it was picked. A preset is the whole sound (every knob and line), not the notes.

hz.preset_delete_ask: Delete the preset "{name}"? The sound you have now stays as it is.

hz.synth_tip_noisy: Noisy: every repeat is late by a random bit. 100 % = up to one whole wave.
hz.synth_tip_vibrato_rate: Rate: how many times a beat the tone goes up and down.
hz.synth_tip_vibrato_depth: Depth: how far the tone goes up and down. 100 % = almost a key each way. 0 = no vibrato.
hz.synth_tip_vibrato_delay: Delay: the vibrato comes in slowly over this long from each note's start, as many singers and synths do. 0 = there at once.
hz.synth_tip_tremolo_rate: Rate: how many times a beat the sound gets quieter and louder again. 0 = no tremolo.
hz.synth_tip_tremolo_depth: Depth: how much quieter it gets. 100 % = down to silence.
hz.synth_tip_wave: Waveform: the shape of each wave. Plain = one note a wave, the brightest sound. Sine = the softest, darkest sound. Square, Triangle and Saw are in between, each with its own colour. A waveform makes up to 16 notes a wave instead of one: the picture below shows them.
hz.synth_tip_shape: Shape: how much of the waveform is used. 0 % = the plain tone, 100 % = the whole waveform (more notes).
hz.synth_tip_octave: Octave below: every other wave gets softer, so the tone an octave lower comes in (like a synth's sub oscillator). No extra notes.
hz.synth_tip_amount: Amount: how many keys up (or down, turned left) each note starts, before it glides to its own tone. 0 = no glide.
hz.synth_tip_time: Time: how long that glide takes.
hz.synth_tip_attack: Attack: how long the sound takes to get loud after you press a key.
hz.synth_tip_decay: Decay: how long it then takes to drop to the Sustain level.
hz.synth_tip_sustain: Sustain: how loud it stays while you hold the key. Above about 50 % it sounds almost the same; changes are easiest to hear in the quiet part.
hz.synth_tip_release: Release: how long it takes to fade out after you let go of the key.
hz.synth_tip_knob: Drag up / down (Shift = fine), mouse wheel or arrow keys. Right mouse button: points it at the mouse. Middle-click = back to the start. Or type a value in the box under it.
hz.synth_drawn: Its lines were drawn by hand (Draw tab), so the knobs only show about where they are. Turning one makes new lines from the knobs.
hz.live_recording: Live keys: recording notes from the soundfont…
hz.live_playing: Live keys: a quick copy, not your MIDI ({mb} MB kept)
hz.live_rough: Live keys: a rough copy, not your MIDI: too many different notes, so every {n} keys play together ({mb} MB kept)
between.title: Add between
between.steps_tip: How many in-between shapes go from the first shape to the last (not counting those two).
between.reverse_tip: Pairs the first shape's start with the last shape's end (and the other way round). Turn it on or off if the steps twist through each other.
between.colours_tip: Every shape of the group gets a channel of its own, the first and last shapes too. Past the number of colours they take turns. Needs Channels: Multi channel. A shape with Colours turned on keeps its own Colours.
between.turns_tip: How many colours the shapes take turns over (at most 15).
between.needs_multi: Channels isn't Multi channel now, so all the steps are in one channel and look the same.
between.hint: Left = the first shape, right = the last. Up = more like the last shape. Each pale line is a step. Drag a point to move it (Shift = free), click the line or empty space to add one, right-click a point to delete it.
between.preview_hint: Blue = the first shape, red = the last. Drag their points to change them (Shift = free); the steps follow.
help.between.title: Add between
help.between.tip: Select two open lines (lines, polylines, curves or arcs), right-click one: Add between…. In-between shapes appear, changing step by step from the first shape into the second. Change one end later and the steps follow.
help.between.text: Select two open lines: lines, polylines, curves or arcs (a joined curve only when its pieces all touch). Right-click one of them: Add between…. Shapes appear between them that change step by step from the first shape (the one that starts earlier) into the second, and a window opens.

In the window: Steps = how many in-between shapes. Reverse pairs the first shape's start with the second's end; switch it if the steps twist through each other. Each shape its own colour gives every shape of the group its own channel, taking turns past the number of colours (needs Channels: Multi channel). The picture at the top shows the group: drag the first or last shape's points to change them. The graph sets how the steps are spread: Even, bunched near the first or last shape, near both ends, or near the middle. OK keeps it all as one undo step, Cancel puts everything back.

The group stays linked: move or reshape the first or last shape and the steps follow. A spot where both shapes are the same (a shared start) stays put in every step. Change a step yourself and it becomes a key shape: the steps on each side change towards it. Right-click a key → Not a key any more makes it a step again.

Velocities, tumours and formulas change step by step too. A tumour or formula only one of the shapes has (or two that can't change into each other) shrinks to nothing by the middle step, then the other one grows from there. Settings that are only on or off switch at the middle step. Claw machine, Strum and Chop pages are kept only when both shapes have the same ones.

The Shapes list shows the group as one row; clicking it selects the whole group. Right-click a shape of the group: Edit add between… (or double-click it), Select the whole group, Unlink. Deleting the first or last shape makes the rest plain shapes. Join, Turn into live shape, Split and Slice unlink the group first. Copying the whole group makes a new group; copying a single step gives a plain shape.
